title.zh: 卷二百六十七 列傳第二十六 張宏 趙昌言 陳恕 魏羽 劉式 劉昌言 張洎 李惟清
title.en: Volume 267 Biographies 26: Zhang Hong, Zhao Changyan, Chen Shu, Wei Yu, Liu Shi, Liu Changyan, Zhang Ji, Li Weiqing
title.raw: 卷二百六十七 列傳第二十六 張宏 趙昌言 陳恕 魏羽 劉式 劉昌言 張洎 李惟清 Volume 267 Biographies 26: Zhang Hong, Zhao Changyan, Chen Shu, Wei Yu, Liu Shi, Liu Changyan, Zhang Ji, Li Weiqing

sentences.zh: 張宏，字巨卿，青州益都人。

translations.literal: Zhang Hong, courtesy name Juqing, was a native of Yidu in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong, styled Juching, was from Yidu in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖茂昭，唐易、定節度使。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Mao Zhao was military commissioner of Yi and Ding under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Mao Zhao had served as military commissioner of Yi and Ding under the Tang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖玄，易州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Xuan was prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Xuan had been prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖持，蒲城令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chi was magistrate of Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chi had been magistrate of Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 父峭，業《春秋》，一舉不第，退居丘園，後唐天成中，以賢帥後，補協律郎，至平利令。

translations.literal: His father Qiao specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He failed to pass the examination on a single attempt and retired to live in seclusion. In the Tiancheng era of Later Tang, because he was descended from a worthy commander, he was appointed Assistant Music Master, and eventually rose to become magistrate of Pingli.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiao devoted himself to the Spring and Autumn Annals. After failing the examinations at his first attempt, he withdrew to private life. During the Tiancheng era of Later Tang, he was appointed Assistant Music Master on the strength of descent from a worthy military commander, and ultimately served as magistrate of Pingli.

sentences.zh: 宏，太平興國二年，舉進士，為將作監丞，通判宣州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, Hong passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and vice prefect of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, Hong passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and vice prefect of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 改太子中允、直史館，遷著作郎，賜緋魚，預修《太平御覽》，歷左拾遺。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Mentor in the Eastern Palace and duty attendant at the Historiography Institute, promoted to Compiler, granted a purple robe and fish tally, participated in compiling the Imperial Readings of the Taiping Era, and served successively as Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Mentor in the Eastern Palace and duty attendant at the Historiography Institute, promoted to Compiler, granted a purple robe and fish tally, took part in compiling the Imperial Readings of the Taiping Era, and served as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 六年，出為峽路轉運副使，就加左補闕、會省副使，知遂州，以勤幹聞，入為度支員外郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was sent out as vice transport commissioner of the Gorges Circuit, concurrently promoted to Left Supplements Counselor and deputy envoy of the Bureau of Accounts, and appointed prefect of Suizhou. Known for diligence and competence, he was recalled to serve as Assistant Director in the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was sent out as vice transport commissioner of the Gorges Circuit, concurrently promoted to Left Supplements Counselor and deputy envoy of the Bureau of Accounts, and appointed prefect of Suizhou. Renowned for diligence and ability, he was recalled to the capital as Assistant Director in the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，呂蒙正、李至、張齊賢、王沔薦其文行，改主客郎中、史館修撰。

translations.literal: During the Yongxi era, Lü Mengzheng, Li Zhi, Zhang Qixian, and Wang Mian recommended him for his literary talent and conduct. He was transferred to Director in the Bureau of Receptions and compiler at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era, Lü Mengzheng, Li Zhi, Zhang Qixian, and Wang Mian recommended him for his literary gifts and character. He was transferred to Director in the Bureau of Receptions and made a compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 數日，以本官充樞密直學士，賜金紫。

translations.literal: Within several days, while retaining his present rank he was appointed confidential academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and granted gold seal with purple sash.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days, while keeping his existing rank, he was appointed confidential academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and granted the gold seal with purple sash.

sentences.zh: 太宗召對便殿，謂曰：「成都重地，卿為朕鎮之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong summoned him for audience in the side hall and said, "Chengdu is a crucial region. You shall govern it on my behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong summoned him to the side hall and said, "Chengdu is a vital post. I want you to hold it for me."

sentences.zh: 因厚賜以遣。

translations.literal: He was then richly rewarded and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then rewarded him generously and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 至鄭州，促召歸闕，拜右諫議大夫、樞密副使。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhengzhou, an urgent summons ordered his return to court. He was appointed Right Remonstrance Counselor and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Zhengzhou, an urgent recall brought him back to court. He was appointed Right Remonstrance Counselor and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會太宗親試禮部不合格貢士，令樞密院給牒，因謂宏曰：「朕自御極以來，親擇群材，大者為棟梁，小者為榱桷，卿與呂蒙正皆中朕選，大臣頗有沮議。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was personally examining civil-service candidates who had failed the Ministry of Rites examination and had the Bureau of Military Affairs issue their credentials. He then said to Hong, "Since I took the throne I have personally chosen talent: the great serve as pillars and beams, the lesser as rafters and purlins. Both you and Lü Mengzheng were among my choices, yet many high ministers strongly objected.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was personally examining civil-service candidates who had failed the Ministry of Rites examination and had the Bureau of Military Affairs issue their credentials. He then said to Hong, "Since I took the throne I have personally chosen talent myself — the great as pillars and beams, the lesser as rafters and purlins. Both you and Lü Mengzheng were among my choices, yet many high ministers strongly objected.

sentences.zh: 非朕獨斷，豈能及此乎？」

translations.literal: Had I not decided alone, how could we have reached this point?"
translations.idiomatic: Had I not decided on my own, how could we have reached this point?"

sentences.zh: 宏頓首謝。

translations.literal: Hong bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Hong bowed his head in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 時河朔用兵，宏居位無所建白，御史中丞趙昌言多言邊事，乃以昌言副樞密，宏為中丞，兩更其任。

translations.literal: When military operations were underway in the Hebei region, Hong in his position offered no constructive proposals, while Censor-in-Chief Zhao Changyan frequently submitted memorials on border affairs. Accordingly Changyan was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Hong Censor-in-Chief, the two exchanging roles.
translations.idiomatic: While the Hebei campaign was underway, Hong offered nothing of substance from his post, whereas Censor-in-Chief Zhao Changyan submitted many memorials on border affairs. The emperor therefore made Changyan Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Hong Censor-in-Chief, the two exchanging positions.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，改工部侍郎，再為樞密副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duan'gong era he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and again appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duan'gong era he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and again made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，以吏部侍郎罷，俄判吏部銓，權知開封府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was dismissed from his post as Vice Minister of Personnel. Shortly thereafter he was assigned to preside over the Ministry of Personnel selection board and given acting charge of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua he was removed as Vice Minister of Personnel. Shortly afterward he was assigned to preside over the Ministry of Personnel selection board and given acting charge of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太宗御便殿慮囚，以府獄多壅，詔劾其官屬，宏等頓首請罪，乃釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor held a prison review in the side hall. Because cases in the prefectural jail were heavily backlogged, he ordered an investigation of the officials. Hong and the others kowtowed begging forgiveness and were then released from blame.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reviewed prisoners in the side hall. Because cases in the prefectural jail were heavily backlogged, he ordered an investigation of the officials. Hong and the others kowtowed begging forgiveness and were released from blame.

sentences.zh: 真宗尹京，宏罷奉朝請。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong served as steward of the capital, Hong was removed from attendance at court.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong served as steward of the capital, Hong was relieved of his court attendance duties.

sentences.zh: 至道初，出知潞州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhidao era he was sent out as prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhidao era he was sent out to serve as prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，就轉右丞。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted in place to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted in place to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加工部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded to the throne, Hong was further promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded to the throne, Hong was further promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，還朝，知審官院、通進銀臺封駁司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he returned to court and was placed in charge of the Bureau of Personnel Evaluation and the Memorial Transmission and Silver Terrace Review Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he returned to court and was placed in charge of the Bureau of Personnel Evaluation and the Memorial Transmission and Silver Terrace Review Office.

sentences.zh: 二年，真宗以上封者眾，慮其稽留，命宏與王旦知登聞鼓院，再掌吏部選。

translations.literal: In the second year, because many memorials were submitted to the throne, Zhenzong feared they would be delayed and ordered Hong and Wang Dan to supervise the Drum and Bell Memorial Office. Hong again took charge of Ministry of Personnel selections.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, because so many memorials were submitted to the throne, Zhenzong feared they would be delayed and ordered Hong and Wang Dan to supervise the Drum and Bell Memorial Office. Hong again took charge of Ministry of Personnel selections.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died at sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，贈右僕射，命中使蒞葬事。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for mourning. He was posthumously appointed Right Grand Counselor, and an imperial envoy was commanded to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for mourning. He was posthumously appointed Right Grand Counselor, and an imperial envoy was ordered to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 錄其子可久大理評事，可道太祝，可度奉禮郎。

translations.literal: His sons Kejiu was appointed Judicial Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, Kedao Grand Supplicator, and Kedu Gentleman for Ceremonial Service.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Kejiu, Kedao, and Kedu were appointed Judicial Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, Grand Supplicator, and Gentleman for Ceremonial Service, respectively.

sentences.zh: 宏循謹守位，不求赫赫之譽，歷踐通顯，未嘗敗事。

translations.literal: Hong was cautious and dutiful in office, never seeking loud renown. Though he rose through illustrious posts, he never failed in his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was cautious and dutiful in office and never sought loud renown. Though he rose through illustrious posts, he never failed in his duties.

sentences.zh: 可久至虞部員外郎，可道國子博士，可度太子中舍。

translations.literal: Kejiu rose to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Public Works, Kedao became Erudite of the National University, and Kedu became Secretary in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Kejiu rose to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Public Works, Kedao became Erudite of the National University, and Kedu became Secretary in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 趙昌言

translations.literal: Zhao Changyan
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Changyan

sentences.zh: 趙昌言，字仲謨，汾州孝義人。

translations.literal: Zhao Changyan, courtesy name Zhongmo, was a native of Xiaoyi in Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Changyan, styled Zhongmo, was from Xiaoyi in Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 父叡，從事使府，太宗尹開封，選為雍丘、太康二縣令，後終安、申觀察判官。

translations.literal: His father Rui served in military governor staffs. When Taizong held stewardship of Kaifeng, Rui was selected as magistrate of both Yongqiu and Taikang counties. He later ended his career as administrative assistant to the military commissioner of An and Shen circuits.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rui served on military governor staffs. When Taizong held stewardship of Kaifeng, Rui was selected as magistrate of both Yongqiu and Taikang counties. He later ended his career as administrative assistant to the military commissioner of An and Shen circuits.

sentences.zh: 昌言少有大志，趙逢、高錫、寇準皆稱許之。

translations.literal: Changyan had great ambitions from youth. Zhao Feng, Gao Xi, and Kou Zhun all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan had great ambitions from youth, and Zhao Feng, Gao Xi, and Kou Zhun all praised him.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，舉進士，文思甚敏，有聲於場屋，為貢部首薦。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination. His literary thought was very nimble and he gained renown in the examination halls, receiving the leading recommendation of the tribute office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination. His literary gifts were very quick, he gained renown in the examination halls, and he received the leading recommendation of the tribute office.

sentences.zh: 廷試日，太宗見其辭氣俊辯，又睹其父名，謂左右曰：「是嘗為東畿宰，朕之生辰，必獻詩百韻為壽，善訓其子，亦為可嘉也。」

translations.literal: On the day of the palace examination the emperor saw how sharp and eloquent his language was. Noticing his father's name as well, he said to those beside him, "This man was once magistrate in the eastern capital region. Every year on my birthday he would present a hundred-rhyme poem as congratulations. He has trained his son well — that too is commendable."
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the palace examination the emperor saw how sharp and eloquent his language was. Noticing his father's name as well, he said to those beside him, "This man was once magistrate in the eastern capital region. Every year on my birthday he would present a hundred-rhyme poem as congratulations. He has trained his son well — that too is commendable."

sentences.zh: 擢置甲科，為將作監丞，通判鄂州。

translations.literal: He was elevated to the first class, appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and made vice prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed in the first class, appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and made vice prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 拜右拾遺、直史館，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Reminder and duty attendant at the Historiography Institute, and granted a purple robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Reminder and duty attendant at the Historiography Institute, and granted a purple robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 選為荊湖轉運副使，遷右補闕，會省副職，改知青州。

translations.literal: He was selected as vice transport commissioner of Jinghu Circuit, promoted to Right Supplements Counselor and deputy envoy of the Bureau of Accounts, then transferred to serve as prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as vice transport commissioner of Jinghu Circuit, promoted to Right Supplements Counselor and deputy envoy of the Bureau of Accounts, then transferred to serve as prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 入拜職方員外郎，知制誥，預修《文苑英華》。

translations.literal: On entering the capital he was appointed Assistant Director in the Bureau of Evaluations, drafter of imperial edicts, and participated in compiling the Finest Blossoms of the Literary Garden.
translations.idiomatic: On entering the capital he was appointed Assistant Director in the Bureau of Evaluations, drafter of imperial edicts, and took part in compiling the Finest Blossoms of the Literary Garden.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，加屯田郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he was further appointed Director in the Bureau of State Farms.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongxi he was further appointed Director in the Bureau of State Farms.

sentences.zh: 明年，同知貢舉，俄出知天雄軍。

translations.literal: The following year he served as co-director of examinations, and shortly afterward was sent out to supervise Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he served as co-director of examinations, and shortly afterward was sent out to supervise Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 時曹彬、崔彥進、米信失律於岐溝，昌言遣觀察支使鄭蒙上疏，請誅彬等。

translations.literal: At that time Cao Bin, Cui Yanjin, and Mi Xin had violated military discipline at Qigou. Changyan had surveillance commissioner aide Zheng Meng submit a memorial calling for the execution of Bin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cao Bin, Cui Yanjin, and Mi Xin had violated military discipline at Qigou. Changyan had surveillance commissioner aide Zheng Meng submit a memorial calling for the execution of Bin and the others.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒答，召拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: An edict praised him in reply. He was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him in reply, and he was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 太宗宴金明池，特召預焉。

translations.literal: When Taizong held a banquet at Jinming Pool, Changyan was specially invited to attend.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong held a banquet at Jinming Pool, Changyan was specially invited to attend.

sentences.zh: 憲官從宴，自昌言始也。

translations.literal: Censorate officials attending banquets began with Changyan.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate officials attending imperial banquets began with Changyan.

sentences.zh: 河朔用兵，樞密副使張宏循默守位，昌言多條上邊事，太宗即以昌言為左諫議大夫，代宏為樞密副使，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: With the Hebei campaign underway, Vice Commissioner Zhang Hong was silent and merely held his position, while Changyan submitted many detailed memorials on border affairs. The emperor thereupon appointed Changyan Left Remonstrance Counselor in place of Hong as Vice Commissioner and promoted him to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: With the Hebei campaign underway, Vice Commissioner Zhang Hong kept silent in his post while Changyan submitted many detailed memorials on border affairs. The emperor thereupon appointed Changyan Left Remonstrance Counselor in place of Hong as Vice Commissioner and promoted him to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時鹽鐵副使陳象輿與昌言善，知制誥胡旦、度支副使董儼皆昌言同年，右正言梁顥嘗在大名幕下。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron Chen Xiangyu was on friendly terms with Changyan. Edict drafter Hu Dan and Vice Commissioner of Revenue Dong Yan were examination classmates of Changyan's. Right Rectifier Liang Hao had once served on the staff at Daming.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron Chen Xiangyu was on friendly terms with Changyan. Edict drafter Hu Dan and Vice Commissioner of Revenue Dong Yan were examination classmates of Changyan's, and Right Rectifier Liang Hao had once served on the staff at Daming.

sentences.zh: 四人者，日夕會昌言之第，京師為之語曰：「陳三更，董半夜。」

translations.literal: These four men met at Changyan's residence day and night. The capital had a saying about them: "Chen at the third watch, Dong at midnight."
translations.idiomatic: These four men met at Changyan's residence day and night. The capital had a saying about them: "Chen at the third watch, Dong at midnight."

sentences.zh: 有傭書翟潁，性險誕，與旦狎，旦為作大言之辭，使潁上之，為潁改姓名馬周，以為唐馬周復出也。

translations.literal: There was a copyist named Zhai Ying, treacherous and deceitful by nature, who was intimate with Hu Dan. Dan composed grandiose words for him and had Ying submit them. For Ying he changed the name to Ma Zhou, thinking that Ma Zhou of Tang had reappeared.
translations.idiomatic: There was a copyist named Zhai Ying, treacherous and deceitful by nature, who was intimate with Hu Dan. Dan composed grandiose words for him and had Ying submit them under the name Ma Zhou, as though Ma Zhou of Tang had reappeared.

sentences.zh: 其言多毀時政，自薦為大臣，及歷舉數十人皆公輔器，期昌言為內應。

translations.literal: The text largely slandered current policy, recommended himself for high office, and successively named dozens of men as material for chief ministers, expecting Changyan to serve as an inside accomplice.
translations.idiomatic: The text largely slandered current policy, recommended himself for high office, and successively named dozens of men as material for chief ministers, expecting Changyan to serve as an inside accomplice.

sentences.zh: 陳王尹開封，廉知以聞，詔捕潁繫獄，鞠之，盡得其狀。

translations.literal: Chen Wang, steward of Kaifeng, discovered this through investigation and reported it. An edict ordered Ying arrested and imprisoned. On interrogation the full circumstances were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wang, steward of Kaifeng, discovered this through investigation and reported it. An edict ordered Ying arrested and imprisoned, and interrogation revealed the full circumstances.

sentences.zh: 昌言坐貶崇信軍節度行軍司馬，潁仗脊黥面，流海島，禁錮終身。

translations.literal: Changyan was demoted to army adjutant on the military commission of Chongxin Circuit. Ying was flogged on the back and tattooed on the face, exiled to an island, and confined for life.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan was demoted to army adjutant on the military commission of Chongxin Circuit. Ying was flogged on the back and tattooed on the face, exiled to an island, and confined for life.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗厚遇昌言，垂欲相之。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had treated Changyan with great favor and was on the verge of making him chief counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had treated Changyan with great favor and was on the verge of making him chief counselor.

sentences.zh: 趙普以勳舊復入，惡昌言剛戾，乃相呂蒙正。

translations.literal: When Zhao Pu returned to court as an old meritorious minister, he disliked Changyan's obstinate sharpness and instead made Lü Mengzheng chief counselor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Pu returned to court as an old meritorious minister, he disliked Changyan's obstinate sharpness and instead made Lü Mengzheng chief counselor.

sentences.zh: 才數月，會有潁獄，普以昌言樹黨，再勸太宗誅之，太宗特寬焉。

translations.literal: Only a few months later, when the Ying case arose, Pu argued that Changyan had formed factions and again urged the emperor to execute him. Taizong showed special lenience.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few months later, when the Ying case arose, Pu argued that Changyan had formed factions and again urged the emperor to execute him. Taizong showed special lenience.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，起昌言知蔡州，逾年，召拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua Changyan was restored and appointed prefect of Caizhou. After more than a year he was summoned and appointed Right Remonstrance Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua Changyan was restored and appointed prefect of Caizhou. After more than a year he was summoned and appointed Right Remonstrance Counselor.

sentences.zh: 或議馳茶鹽禁，以省轉漕。

translations.literal: Some proposed lifting the tea and salt monopolies to reduce transport costs.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed lifting the tea and salt monopolies to reduce transport costs.

sentences.zh: 命昌言為江淮、兩浙制置茶鹽使，昌言極言非便，太宗不納，趣昌言往。

translations.literal: Changyan was appointed commissioner for establishing tea and salt policy in Jianghuai and the two Zhe circuits. He strongly argued the move was unwise. The emperor did not accept this and urged him to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan was appointed commissioner for establishing tea and salt policy in Jianghuai and the two Zhe circuits. He strongly argued the move was unwise, but the emperor did not accept this and urged him to depart.

sentences.zh: 昌言固執如初。

translations.literal: Changyan held firm as before.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan held firm as before.

sentences.zh: 即以戶部副使雷有終代之，卒以無利而罷。

translations.literal: Lei Youzhong, Vice Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue, was immediately sent to replace him. In the end the proposal brought no profit and was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Youzhong, Vice Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue, was immediately sent to replace him. In the end the proposal brought no profit and was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 昌言復知天雄軍，賜錢二百萬。

translations.literal: Changyan again served as supervisor of Tianxiong Army and was granted two million cash.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan again served as supervisor of Tianxiong Army and was granted two million cash.

sentences.zh: 大河貫府境，豪民峙芻茭圖利，誘奸人潛穴堤防，歲仍決溢。

translations.literal: The Yellow River ran through the prefecture. Powerful locals hoarded fodder for profit and induced evildoers to secretly burrow into the dikes, so that each year the river still broke its banks.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River ran through the prefecture. Powerful locals hoarded fodder for profit and induced evildoers to secretly burrow into the dikes, so that each year the river still broke its banks.

sentences.zh: 昌言知之。

translations.literal: Changyan knew of this.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan knew of this.

sentences.zh: 一日，堤吏告急，命徑取豪家廥積以給用，自是無敢為姦利者。

translations.literal: One day when dike officials reported an emergency, he ordered fodder taken directly from wealthy households' stored supplies for use. From then on none dared seek illicit profit.
translations.idiomatic: One day when dike officials reported an emergency, he ordered fodder taken directly from wealthy households' stored supplies for use. From then on none dared seek illicit profit.

sentences.zh: 屬澶州河決，流入御河，漲溢浸府城，昌言籍府兵負土增堤，數不及千，乃索禁卒佐役，皆偃蹇不進。

translations.literal: When the river broke its banks at Cizhou and flowed into the imperial canal, swelling and inundating the prefectural city, Changyan conscripted prefectural troops to carry earth and raise the dikes. Their number fell short of a thousand, so he summoned palace guard soldiers to assist. All hung back and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the river broke its banks at Cizhou and flowed into the imperial canal, swelling and inundating the prefectural city, Changyan conscripted prefectural troops to carry earth and raise the dikes. Their number fell short of a thousand, so he summoned palace guard soldiers to assist. All hung back and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 昌言怒曰：「府城將墊，人民且溺，汝輩食厚祿，欲坐觀耶？

translations.literal: Changyan angrily said, "The prefectural city is about to collapse and the people will drown. You enjoy rich salaries — do you mean to sit by and watch?
translations.idiomatic: Changyan angrily said, "The prefectural city is about to collapse and the people will drown. You enjoy rich salaries — do you mean to sit by and watch?

sentences.zh: 敢不從命者斬。」

translations.literal: Whoever dares disobey shall be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever dares disobey shall be executed."

sentences.zh: 眾股慄赴役，不浹旬城完。

translations.literal: The men trembled and hurried to the work. Within less than ten days the city walls were secure.
translations.idiomatic: The men trembled and hurried to the work. Within less than ten days the city walls were secure.

sentences.zh: 太宗手詔褒諭之，召拜給事中、參知政事，俾乘疾置以入，即赴中書。

translations.literal: Taizong personally wrote an edict praising him, summoned him, and appointed him Gentleman Attendant and Assistant Administrator of Affairs. He was ordered to enter by express relay and proceed directly to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong personally wrote an edict praising him, summoned him, and appointed him Gentleman Attendant and Assistant Administrator of Affairs. He was ordered to enter by express relay and proceed directly to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時京城連雨，昌言請出廄馬分牧外郡。

translations.literal: When the capital suffered continuous rain, Changyan requested that imperial stud horses be sent out to graze in outer prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital suffered continuous rain, Changyan requested that imperial stud horses be sent out to graze in outer prefectures.

sentences.zh: 或以盛秋備敵，馬不可闕。

translations.literal: Some argued that in the height of autumn they must prepare against the enemy and the horses could not be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that in the height of autumn they must prepare against the enemy and the horses could not be spared.

sentences.zh: 昌言曰：「塞下積水，敵必不至。」

translations.literal: Changyan said, "The frontier is flooded — the enemy certainly will not come."
translations.idiomatic: Changyan said, "The frontier is flooded — the enemy certainly will not come."

sentences.zh: 太宗從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 未幾，王小波、李順構亂於蜀，議遣大臣撫慰。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Xiaobo and Li Shun raised rebellion in Shu. The court debated sending a high minister to console the region.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Xiaobo and Li Shun raised rebellion in Shu. The court debated sending a high minister to console the region.

sentences.zh: 昌言獨請發兵，無使滋蔓，廷論未決。

translations.literal: Changyan alone requested dispatch of troops so the disorder would not spread. Court discussion remained unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan alone requested dispatch of troops so the disorder would not spread. Court discussion remained unresolved.

sentences.zh: 會嘉、眉連陷，始命王繼恩等分路進討。

translations.literal: When Jia and Mei fell in succession, Wang Jien and others were finally ordered to advance along separate routes to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia and Mei fell in succession, Wang Jien and others were finally ordered to advance along separate routes to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 昌言攝祭太廟，宿齋中，因召對滋福殿，復贊兵計，遂遣使督繼恩戰。

translations.literal: Changyan officiated at a temple sacrifice, lodged in the fasting quarters, and was summoned for audience in Zifu Hall. He again urged a military plan, and an envoy was sent to supervise Jien's campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan officiated at a temple sacrifice, lodged in the fasting quarters, and was summoned for audience in Zifu Hall. He again urged a military plan, and an envoy was sent to supervise Jien's campaign.

sentences.zh: 繼恩御眾寡術，餘寇未殄，握兵留成都，士無鬥志，郡縣復有陷者。

translations.literal: Jien lacked skill in commanding large or small forces. Remaining bandits had not been destroyed. He kept his army at Chengdu and the soldiers lost fighting spirit; prefectures and counties again fell.
translations.idiomatic: Jien lacked skill in commanding large or small forces. Remaining bandits had not been destroyed. He kept his army at Chengdu and the soldiers lost fighting spirit; prefectures and counties again fell.

sentences.zh: 太宗意頗厭兵，召昌言謂曰：「西川本自一國，太祖平之，訖今三十年矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor grew weary of the campaign and summoned Changyan, saying, "Western Sichuan was originally a separate state. Taizu pacified it, and it has now been thirty years."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew weary of the campaign and summoned Changyan, saying, "Western Sichuan was originally a separate state. Taizu pacified it, and it has now been thirty years."

sentences.zh: 昌言知意，即前指畫攻取之策。

translations.literal: Understanding his meaning, Changyan immediately stepped forward and outlined a plan for capture by assault.
translations.idiomatic: Understanding his meaning, Changyan immediately stepped forward and outlined a plan for capture by assault.

sentences.zh: 太宗喜，命昌言為川峽五十二州招安行營馬步軍都部署。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and appointed Changyan overall commander of the Pacification Army for the fifty-two prefectures of Sichuan and the Gorges.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and appointed Changyan overall commander of the Pacification Army for the fifty-two prefectures of Sichuan and the Gorges.

sentences.zh: 昌言懇辭，敦諭不許，賜精鎧、良馬、白金五千兩，別賜手劄數幅，皆討賊方略。

translations.literal: Changyan earnestly declined but repeated persuasion was refused. He was granted fine armor, good horses, and five thousand taels of silver, and separately given several personal letters, all containing strategy for suppressing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan earnestly declined but repeated persuasion was refused. He was granted fine armor, good horses, and five thousand taels of silver, and separately given several personal letters, all containing strategy for suppressing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 自繼恩以下，並受節度。

translations.literal: From Jien downward, all were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: From Jien downward, all were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 既行，有奏昌言無嗣，鼻折山根，頗有反相，不宜遣握兵入蜀。

translations.literal: After he departed, a memorial reported that Changyan had no son, that his nose was crooked at the bridge with features suggesting rebellion, and that he should not be sent to command troops into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After he departed, a memorial reported that Changyan had no son, that his nose was crooked at the bridge with features suggesting rebellion, and that he should not be sent to command troops into Shu.

sentences.zh: 後旬日，召宰相於北苑門曰：「昨令昌言入蜀，朕思之有所未便。

translations.literal: Some ten days later the emperor summoned the chief counselors at the North Garden Gate and said, "Yesterday I ordered Changyan into Shu, but on reflection I find it somewhat unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: Some ten days later the emperor summoned the chief counselors at the North Garden Gate and said, "Yesterday I ordered Changyan into Shu, but on reflection I find it somewhat unsuitable.

sentences.zh: 且蜀賊小醜，昌言大臣，未易前進。

translations.literal: Moreover the Shu rebels are petty bandits, while Changyan is a great minister — it is not easy for him to go forward.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Shu rebels are petty bandits, while Changyan is a great minister — it is not easy for him to go forward.

sentences.zh: 且令駐鳳翔，止遣內侍衛紹欽齎手書指揮軍事，亦可濟也。」

translations.literal: Instead let him halt at Fengxiang and send only palace attendant Shao Qin with personal letters to direct military affairs — that too will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Instead let him halt at Fengxiang and send only palace attendant Shao Qin with personal letters to direct military affairs — that too will suffice."

sentences.zh: 詔書追及，昌言已至鳳州，留候館百餘日。

translations.literal: The pursuing edict reached him when he had already arrived at Fengzhou. He remained at the relay station for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuing edict reached him when he had already arrived at Fengzhou. He remained at the relay station for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 賊平，改戶部侍郎，罷政事，知鳳翔府。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, removed from administration, and appointed prefect of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, removed from administration, and appointed prefect of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 徙澶、涇、延三州。

translations.literal: He was transferred among the prefectures of Cao, Jing, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred among the prefectures of Cao, Jing, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，遷兵部侍郎、知陝州，表求還京，不許。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded to the throne Changyan was transferred to Vice Minister of War and appointed prefect of Shaanzhou. He memorialized requesting return to the capital but was denied.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded to the throne Changyan was transferred to Vice Minister of War and appointed prefect of Shaanzhou. He memorialized requesting return to the capital but was denied.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移知永興軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to supervise Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to supervise Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，與呂蒙正、寇準同召，以本官兼御史中丞、知審官院。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping he was summoned together with Lü Mengzheng and Kou Zhun, retaining his present rank while also serving as Censor-in-Chief and director of the Bureau of Personnel Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping he was summoned together with Lü Mengzheng and Kou Zhun, retaining his present rank while also serving as Censor-in-Chief and director of the Bureau of Personnel Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 有言門資官不宜任親民，昌言手疏，以才不才在人，豈以寒進世家為限，遂罷其議。

translations.literal: Some argued that officials of hereditary pedigree should not hold posts governing the people directly. Changyan submitted a personal memorial arguing that talent or lack of it lies in the person — how could one be limited by humble origin or noble lineage? The proposal was therefore dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that officials of hereditary pedigree should not hold posts governing the people directly. Changyan submitted a personal memorial arguing that talent or lack of it lies in the person — how could one be limited by humble origin or noble lineage? The proposal was therefore dropped.

sentences.zh: 加工部尚書，仍兼中丞。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Minister of Works while still serving concurrently as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Minister of Works while still serving concurrently as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 先時，多遣臺吏巡察群臣逾越法式者，昌言建議請準故事，令左右巡使分領之。

translations.literal: Earlier many censorate clerks had been sent to inspect officials who exceeded proper regulations. Changyan proposed following precedent and having left and right touring commissioners divide responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier many censorate clerks had been sent to inspect officials who exceeded proper regulations. Changyan proposed following precedent and having left and right touring commissioners divide responsibility.

sentences.zh: 會知審刑院趙安仁、判大理寺韓國華斷獄失中解職，昌言因上言：「詳斷官宜加慎擇，自今有議刑不當，嚴示懲罰，授以遠官，若有罪被問不即引伏者，許令追攝。

translations.literal: When Zhao Anren, director of the Bureau of Judicial Review, and Han Guohua, chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, were removed for incorrect judgments, Changyan submitted a memorial: "Judges who examine cases should be chosen with extra care. From now on when a sentence is judged improper, strict punishment should be shown — appointment to a distant post. If one accused of a crime under questioning does not promptly confess, he may be pursued and seized.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Anren, director of the Bureau of Judicial Review, and Han Guohua, chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, were removed for incorrect judgments, Changyan submitted a memorial: "Judges who examine cases should be chosen with extra care. From now on when a sentence is judged improper, strict punishment should be shown — appointment to a distant post. If one accused of a crime under questioning does not promptly confess, he may be pursued and seized.

sentences.zh: 又天下大辟斷訖，皆錄款聞奏，付刑部詳覆，用刑乖理者皆行按劾。

translations.literal: Furthermore, after all capital cases nationwide are decided, the records of confession should be reported to the throne, sent to the Ministry of Justice for detailed review, and anyone whose use of punishment violated reason should be investigated and impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, after all capital cases nationwide are decided, the records of confession should be reported to the throne, sent to the Ministry of Justice for detailed review, and anyone whose use of punishment violated reason should be investigated and impeached.

sentences.zh: 惟開封府未嘗奏案，或斷獄有失，止罪元勘官吏，知府、判官、推官、檢法官皆不及責，則何以辨明枉濫，表則方夏？

translations.literal: Only Kaifeng Prefecture has never reported cases. If a judgment errs, only the original investigating officials are punished — the prefect, assistant prefect, examining magistrate, and judicial examiner all escape liability. How then can wrongful convictions be distinguished and corrected, and a standard set for the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Only Kaifeng Prefecture has never reported its cases upward. When a judgment goes wrong, punishment stops at the original investigating clerks, while the prefect, assistant prefect, examining magistrate, and judicial examiner all escape blame. How, then, can wrongful convictions be exposed and corrected, or the capital set an example for the entire realm?

sentences.zh: 望自今如外州例施行。」

translations.literal: It is hoped that from now on the practice of outer prefectures will be applied."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from now on Kaifeng follow the same procedure used in the outer prefectures."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 會孟州民常德方訟臨津尉任懿以賄登第，事下御史，乃知舉王欽若受之，昌言以聞。

translations.literal: Meanwhile a Mengzhou commoner named Chang Defang sued Assistant Magistrate Ren Yi of Linjin for buying his way to passing the examination. The case went to the censorate, revealing that chief examiner Wang Qinruo had accepted the bribe. Changyan reported this to the court.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that a commoner of Mengzhou named Chang Defang sued Ren Yi, assistant magistrate of Linjin, for having passed the examinations by bribery. When the case reached the censorate, it emerged that the chief examiner Wang Qinruo had taken the bribe. Changyan reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 欽若自訴，詔刑昺覆按，坐昌言故入，奪官，貶安遠軍行軍司馬，移武勝軍。

translations.literal: Qinruo lodged his own appeal. An edict ordered Xing Bing to reinvestigate. Changyan was found guilty of intentional misapplication, stripped of office, demoted to army affairs staff officer of Anyuan Army, and transferred to Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo appealed in his own defense. The emperor ordered Xing Bing to reinvestigate. Changyan was convicted of intentional wrongful conviction, stripped of rank, demoted to army affairs staff officer of Anyuan Army, and later transferred to Wusheng Army.

sentences.zh: 景德初，拜刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingde era he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 求兼三館職，命判尚書都省。

translations.literal: He requested a concurrent post in the Three Institutes and was ordered to serve as director of the Secretariat Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He sought a concurrent appointment in the Three Institutes and was ordered to direct the Secretariat Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 真宗幸澶淵，以盟津居要，增屯兵，命知河陽。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong visited Chanyuan, because Mengjin occupied a strategic position troops were increased. He was appointed prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong traveled to Chanyuan, Mengjin was judged a key position and additional troops were stationed there. Changyan was appointed prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 歷知天雄軍府。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of the Tianxiong Military Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of the Tianxiong Military Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 境內有小盜，昌言榜諭能告賊者給賞，牙吏即遷職。

translations.literal: When small bandits appeared within the jurisdiction, Changyan posted notices offering rewards to whoever could report bandits, and yamen clerks would be immediately promoted.
translations.idiomatic: When petty bandits appeared in his jurisdiction, Changyan posted notices promising rewards to anyone who informed on them, with immediate promotion for the reporting clerks.

sentences.zh: 樞密使王繼英以為小盜不當擅為賞格，乃詔昌言易其榜，有勞者俟朝旨。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Jiying held that rewards for petty theft should not be offered on one's own authority, so an edict ordered Changyan to replace his notice — those with merit should await imperial instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Jiying argued that rewards for petty banditry should not be set unilaterally, so an edict ordered Changyan to replace his notice: anyone deserving reward would have to await the court's decision.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙知鎮州，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to prefect of Zhenzhou and promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to serve as prefect of Zhenzhou and promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died at sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，諡曰景肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel and given the posthumous title Jingsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel and given the posthumous title Jingsu, "Solemn and Reverent."

sentences.zh: 錄其子慶嗣為國子監丞，賦祿終喪。

translations.literal: His son Qingsi was appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Education, with salary granted until mourning ended.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qingsi was appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Education, with a stipend granted through the end of mourning.

sentences.zh: 侄孫允明同學究出身。

translations.literal: His grand-nephew Yunming received office through the xiue jiu route.
translations.idiomatic: His grand-nephew Yunming entered service as a classicist graduate.

sentences.zh: 昌言喜推獎後進，掌漕湖外時，李沆通判潭州，昌言謂有臺輔之量，表聞於朝。

translations.literal: Changyan delighted in recommending rising talent. While serving as transport commissioner outside the lake region, Li Hang was vice prefect of Tanzhou. Changyan considered him to have the capacity for high censorate and council posts and memorialized the court.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan loved to promote rising talent. While serving as transport commissioner for the region beyond the lakes, he met Li Hang, vice prefect of Tanzhou, judged him fit for the highest censorate and council posts, and memorialized the court on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 王旦宰岳州平江，昌言一見，識其遠大，以女妻之，後皆為賢相。

translations.literal: Wang Dan was magistrate of Pingjiang in Yuezhou. At one meeting Changyan recognized his far-reaching potential and gave him his daughter in marriage. Both later became worthy chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan was magistrate of Pingjiang in Yuezhou. At their first meeting Changyan recognized his great promise and gave him his daughter in marriage. Both men later became celebrated chancellors.

sentences.zh: 王禹偁自卑秩擢詞職，亦昌言所薦也。

translations.literal: Wang Yucheng was promoted from a low rank to a literary post — this too was by Changyan's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yucheng's promotion from a humble rank to a literary post was also due to Changyan's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 昌言強力尚氣概，當官無所顧避，所至以威斷立名，雖屢經擯斥，未嘗少自抑損。

translations.literal: Changyan was forceful and valued bold spirit. Holding office he showed no evasion, and wherever he went he established a reputation through stern judgment. Though repeatedly dismissed and rejected, he never slightly diminished himself.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan was forceful and proud of spirit. In office he held nothing back, and wherever he served he made a name for stern decisiveness. Though repeatedly cast out and demoted, he never once lowered himself.

sentences.zh: 然剛愎縱率，對僚吏倨慢，時論以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet he was stubborn, willful, and unrestrained; toward colleagues and subordinates he was haughty and cold, and contemporary opinion counted this against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was obstinate, willful, and unrestrained, haughty and dismissive toward colleagues and subordinates, and contemporary opinion held this against him.

sentences.zh: 慶嗣至太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Qingsi rose to Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Qingsi rose to the post of Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 陳恕，字仲言，洪州南昌人。

translations.literal: Chen Shu, courtesy name Zhongyan, was a native of Nanchang in Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shu, styled Zhongyan, was a native of Nanchang in Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 少為縣吏，折節讀書。

translations.literal: In youth he was a county clerk; he reformed himself and took up reading.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served as a county clerk, then disciplined himself and turned to study.

sentences.zh: 江南平，禮部侍郎王明知洪州，恕以儒服見，明與語，大奇之，因資送令預計偕。

translations.literal: When the Jiangnan region was pacified, Wang Ming, Vice Minister of Rites, governed Hongzhou. Shu came to see him in scholar's garb. Ming conversed with him and was greatly struck, and so provided funds and ordered him to take the prefectural qualifying examination.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiangnan region was pacified, Wang Ming, Vice Minister of Rites, governed Hongzhou. Shu came to see him dressed as a scholar. Wang spoke with him, was deeply impressed, provided him funds, and had him sit for the prefectural qualifying examination.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年進士，解褐大理評事、通判洪州，恕以鄉里辭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination. Upon entering service he was appointed Judicial Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and vice prefect of Hongzhou. Shu declined on account of his home district.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination and upon entering service was appointed Judicial Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and vice prefect of Hongzhou. Shu declined on account of his home district.

sentences.zh: 改澧州。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to serve as vice prefect of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 澧自唐季為節鎮兼領，吏多緣簿書乾沒為姦。

translations.literal: Lizhou since the late Tang had been a military commissioner's seat with a concurrent command — clerks often used their familiarity with records to embezzle and commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Since the late Tang Lizhou had been the seat of a military commissioner, and clerks often exploited their control of the ledgers to embezzle and commit fraud.

sentences.zh: 恕盡擿發其弊，郡中稱為強明，以吏幹聞。

translations.literal: Shu fully exposed these abuses. Within the prefecture he was acclaimed as forceful and perceptive, and became known for administrative competence.
translations.idiomatic: Shu exposed every abuse he could find. The prefecture hailed him as forceful and clear-sighted, and his reputation for administrative skill spread.

sentences.zh: 召入，為右讚善大夫，同判三司勾院，遷左拾遺，充度支判官。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, he was made Right Supporter of Excellence Grandee, concurrently adjutant of the Bureau of Accounts Audit Office of the Three Directorates, promoted to Left Collector of Omissions, and appointed revenue section judge.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he was appointed Right Supporter of Excellence Grandee and adjutant of the Bureau of Accounts Audit Office of the Three Directorates, then promoted to Left Collector of Omissions and appointed revenue section judge.

sentences.zh: 與判使王仁贍廷爭本司事，仁贍屈伏，坐貶秩；

translations.literal: He disputed at court with Commissioner Wang Renzan over matters of the directorate. Renzan bowed before his argument and was demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He argued before the throne with Commissioner Wang Renzan over affairs of the directorate. Renzan was overborne and demoted in rank;

sentences.zh: 擢恕為度支員外郎，仍舊職。

translations.literal: Shu was promoted to Assistant Director in the Bureau of Revenue, retaining his former duties.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was promoted to Assistant Director in the Bureau of Revenue while retaining his existing duties.

sentences.zh: 再遷工部郎中、知大名府。

translations.literal: Promoted again to Director in the Ministry of Works and prefect of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Director in the Ministry of Works and appointed prefect of Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時契丹內寇，受詔增浚城隍，其器用取於民者不時集，恕立擒府中大豪一人，會將吏將斬之。

translations.literal: At the time the Khitans raided within the borders. He received orders to deepen and repair city moats and walls. Materials requisitioned from the people were not assembled in time. Shu immediately arrested one leading local magnate in the prefecture, assembled the staff officers, and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Khitans were raiding within the borders. Ordered to deepen the moats and repair the walls, he found that requisitioned materials from the populace were not arriving on time. Shu immediately seized one leading local magnate in the prefecture, assembled the staff officers, and prepared to execute him.

sentences.zh: 宗族號訴，賓佐競前請救，大豪叩頭流血，請翌日集事，違期甘死。

translations.literal: The clan wailed and appealed. Assistants and aides rushed forward begging mercy. The magnate kowtowed until he bled and asked to gather the materials the next day, promising that if he missed the deadline he would gladly accept death.
translations.idiomatic: The man's clansmen wailed and pleaded. Assistants and aides rushed forward to beg for his life. The magnate kowtowed until his forehead bled, asking for one more day to gather the materials and swearing that if he missed the deadline he would accept death without complaint.

sentences.zh: 恕令械之以徇，民皆恐慄，無敢後期者，數日功就。

translations.literal: Shu ordered him shackled and paraded as a warning. The people all trembled with fear and none dared miss the deadline. Within days the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had him shackled and paraded as a warning. The people trembled with fear, none dared miss the deadline, and within days the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 會契丹引去，召入為戶部郎中、戶部副使，遷右諫議大夫、知澶州。

translations.literal: When the Khitans withdrew, he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Revenue and deputy commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue, then promoted to Right Remonstrance Counselor and prefect of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans withdrew, he was recalled as Director in the Ministry of Revenue and deputy commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue, then promoted to Right Remonstrance Counselor and appointed prefect of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 驛召為河北東路營田制置使。

translations.literal: He was urgently recalled by courier post as commissioner for military farming in the Hebei Eastern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was urgently recalled by courier post and appointed commissioner for military farming on the Hebei Eastern Circuit.

sentences.zh: 太宗諭以農戰之旨，恕對曰：「古者兵出於民，無寇則耕，寇至則戰。

translations.literal: Taizong instructed him on the principle of farming and fighting. Shu replied: "In antiquity soldiers came from the people — when no enemy appeared they farmed; when enemies came they fought.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong explained the principle of combining farming and warfare. Shu replied, "In antiquity soldiers came from the people: when there was no enemy they farmed; when enemies came they fought.

sentences.zh: 今之戎士皆以募致，衣食仰給縣官，若使之冬持兵禦寇，春執耒服田，萬一生變，悔無及矣。」

translations.literal: Today's warriors are all recruited and equipped. Their food and clothing rely on the district treasury. If they were made to hold weapons against raiders in winter and take plows to the fields in spring, should any disturbance arise it would be too late for regret."
translations.idiomatic: Today's soldiers are all recruited men whose food and clothing depend on the state treasury. If they were made to bear arms against raiders in winter and take up the plow in spring, the slightest disturbance would come too late to remedy."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「卿第行，朕思之。」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "You need only go — I will reconsider."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Go for now — I will think it over."

sentences.zh: 恕行數日，果有詔，止令修完城堡、通導溝瀆而已，營田之議遂寢。

translations.literal: After Shu had been on the road several days, an edict indeed arrived ordering only the repair of fortifications and dredging of canals — the military-farming proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu had traveled several days, an edict indeed arrived ordering only the repair of fortifications and dredging of canals. The military-farming proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 俄知代州，入判吏部選事，拜鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Daizhou, entered to serve as judge of Ministry of Personnel selections, and was appointed salt and iron commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed prefect of Daizhou, then entered court to judge Ministry of Personnel selections and was appointed salt and iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 恕有心計，釐去宿弊，太宗深器之，親題殿柱曰「真鹽鐵陳恕」。

translations.literal: Shu was resourceful in planning. He cleared away longstanding abuses. Taizong greatly valued him and personally wrote on a palace pillar: "The True Salt and Iron Commissioner Chen Shu."
translations.idiomatic: Shu was shrewd and resourceful. He cleared away longstanding abuses, and Taizong valued him deeply, personally inscribing a palace pillar: "The True Salt and Iron Commissioner Chen Shu."

sentences.zh: 遷給事中、參知政事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Censor and Vice Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Censor and appointed Vice Councilor.

sentences.zh: 數月，太宗言及戶部使樊知古所部不治。

translations.literal: Several months later Taizong spoke of how Fan Zhigu's supervision of the Ministry of Revenue office was poorly managed.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later Taizong remarked that Fan Zhigu's supervision of the Ministry of Revenue office was in poor order.

sentences.zh: 恕與知古聯事，情好款洽，密以語之，欲知古修舉其職。

translations.literal: Shu worked closely with Zhigu and was on intimate terms; he secretly told him, hoping Zhigu would properly perform his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Shu worked closely with Zhigu and was on friendly terms with him. He secretly passed the remark along, hoping Zhigu would reform and properly perform his duties.

sentences.zh: 知古訴於太宗，太宗怒恕泄禁中語，罷守本官。

translations.literal: Zhigu complained to Taizong. Taizong was angry that Shu had leaked words from within the palace and removed him to retain his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu complained to Taizong. Taizong was furious that Shu had leaked words spoken within the palace and removed him from the council, allowing him to retain his original rank.

sentences.zh: 旋出知江陵府，大發群吏姦贓，坐徒、流、停、廢者甚眾，郡內惕息。

translations.literal: Shortly he was sent out as prefect of Jiangling Prefecture. He broadly exposed the graft of the clerical staff. Very many were sentenced to exile, banishment, suspension, or dismissal. Within the prefecture everyone was subdued.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as prefect of Jiangling Prefecture, where he broadly exposed clerical corruption. Very many were sentenced to penal service, exile, suspension, or dismissal, and the whole prefecture fell silent with fear.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，太宗從魏羽、段惟一之請，分三司為十道，置左右計使，以魏羽、董儼分主之；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua, following the request of Wei Yu and Duan Weiyi, Taizong divided the Three Directorates into ten circuits and established left and right planning commissioners, with Wei Yu and Dong Yan each overseeing one.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua, at the request of Wei Yu and Duan Weiyi, Taizong divided the Three Directorates into ten circuits and established left and right planning commissioners, with Wei Yu and Dong Yan placed in charge;

sentences.zh: 召恕為工部侍郎，充總計使，判左右計事。

translations.literal: Shu was summoned as Vice Minister of Works, appointed chief planning commissioner with concurrent adjudication of left and right planning affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was summoned as Vice Minister of Works, appointed chief planning commissioner, and given concurrent authority over left and right planning affairs.

sentences.zh: 左右計使分判十道事，凡議論、計度並令恕等參預。

translations.literal: Left and right planning commissioners each divided management of the ten circuits. All deliberations and calculations were also to involve Shu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right planning commissioners each oversaw affairs in the ten circuits, and all deliberations and calculations were also to involve Shu and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 恕以官司各建，政令互出，難以經久，極言其非便。

translations.literal: Shu argued that because each agency was separately established and orders overlapped, the system could not last — he strongly stated the inconvenience.
translations.idiomatic: Shu argued that with separate agencies issuing overlapping orders the arrangement could not last, and he strongly stated its drawbacks.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，果罷，復以恕為鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: After a little over a year the arrangement was indeed abolished, and Shu was again made salt and iron commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year the arrangement was abolished as he had predicted, and Shu was again appointed salt and iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時太宗留意金穀，召三司吏李溥等二十七人對於崇政殿，詢以計司利害。

translations.literal: At the time Taizong attended closely to revenue. He summoned twenty-seven clerks of the Three Directorates, including Li Pu, for audience in the Chongzheng Hall and inquired about the advantages and disadvantages of the accounting offices.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Taizong was closely attentive to revenue. He summoned twenty-seven clerks of the Three Directorates, including Li Pu, to audience in the Chongzheng Hall and questioned them about the strengths and weaknesses of the accounting offices.

sentences.zh: 溥等言條目煩多，不可以口占，願給筆劄以對。

translations.literal: Pu and the others said the regulations were too numerous to recount orally and requested writing materials to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and the others said the regulations were too numerous to recite orally and asked for writing materials so they could reply in writing.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣中黃門送詣相府，限五日悉條上之。

translations.literal: Taizong sent palace eunuchs to escort them to the chief councilor's office with a five-day limit to list everything and submit it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent palace eunuchs to escort them to the chief councilor's office and gave them five days to list everything and submit it upward.

sentences.zh: 溥等共上七十一事，詔以四十四事付有司行之，其十九事下恕等議可否。

translations.literal: Pu and the others together submitted seventy-one items. An edict ordered forty-four put into practice through the relevant offices; nineteen were sent down to Shu and others to discuss feasibility.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and the others together submitted seventy-one items. An edict ordered forty-four implemented through the relevant offices; the remaining nineteen were sent down to Shu and others to discuss whether they should be adopted.

sentences.zh: 遣知雜御史張秉、中使張崇貴監議，令中書籍其事，專檢舉之，無致廢格。

translations.literal: Supervising censor Zhang Bing and palace envoy Zhang Chonggui were dispatched to oversee the deliberations, ordering the Secretariat to record the matter and oversee implementation without letting it fall idle.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Zhang Bing and palace envoy Zhang Chonggui were dispatched to oversee the deliberations. The Secretariat was ordered to record the matter, monitor implementation, and see that nothing was allowed to lapse.

sentences.zh: 賜溥等白金緡錢，悉補侍禁、殿直，領其職。

translations.literal: Pu and the others were granted platinum cash. All were appointed as palace attendants or inner hall duty officers to take charge of their respective posts.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and the others were granted platinum cash. All were appointed palace attendants or inner hall duty officers and put in charge of their respective duties.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂宰相曰：「溥等條奏事頗有所長。

translations.literal: Taizong said to the chief councilors: "Pu and the others' memorialized items indeed show certain strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said to the chief councilors, "In their memorialized items Pu and the others indeed show real strengths.

sentences.zh: 朕嘗語恕等，若文章稽古，此輩固不可望；

translations.literal: I have told Shu and the others that in classical learning and antiquarian scholarship these men certainly cannot be hoped for;
translations.idiomatic: I have told Shu and the others that in classical learning and antiquarian scholarship one certainly cannot expect such men;

sentences.zh: 若錢穀利病，頗自幼至長，寢處其中，必周知根本。

translations.literal: but in fiscal advantages and defects, from youth through old age dwelling within the work, they must thoroughly know the fundamentals.
translations.idiomatic: but in fiscal strengths and weaknesses, having lived within the work from youth to old age, they must know the fundamentals through and through.

sentences.zh: 卿等但假以顏色，引令剖陳，必有所益。

translations.literal: You need only show them a friendly countenance and lead them to lay out their views — there will surely be benefit.
translations.idiomatic: You need only receive them warmly and draw them out to explain their views — there will surely be benefit.

sentences.zh: 恕等剛強，終不肯降意詢問。」

translations.literal: Shu and the others are rigid and in the end refuse to lower themselves to inquire."
translations.idiomatic: But Shu and the others are stiff-necked and refuse to lower themselves to ask."

sentences.zh: 呂端對曰：「耕當問奴，織當問婢。」

translations.literal: Lü Duan replied: "When plowing one should ask the slave; when weaving one should ask the maid."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Duan replied, "When plowing one should ask the farmhand; when weaving one should ask the maid."

sentences.zh: 寇準曰：「夫子入太廟，每事問，乃以貴下賤，先有司之義。」

translations.literal: Kou Zhun said: "When the Master entered the temple he inquired about every matter — this is using the honored to defer to the lowly, the meaning of letting specialists take charge first."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun said, "When the Master entered the temple he asked about every rite — that is the noble deferring to the humble, the principle of letting those in charge go first."

sentences.zh: 後數日，太宗又曰：「國家歲入財數倍於唐。

translations.literal: Several days later Taizong again said: "The state's yearly revenue is several times that of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Taizong again said, "The state's annual revenue is several times that of the Tang.

sentences.zh: 唐中葉以降，藩鎮擅命，征賦多不入公家，下陵上替，經制隳壞。

translations.literal: From mid-Tang onward military commissioners held autonomous power and much taxation never entered the public treasury. Subordinates undermined superiors and institutional order collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: From mid-Tang onward military commissioners held autonomous power, much taxation never reached the public treasury, subordinates undermined superiors, and institutional order collapsed.

sentences.zh: 若前代為得，即已致太平，豈復煩朕心慮也。」

translations.literal: If the former age had been correct, peace would already have been achieved — why would it still vex my heart and thought?"
translations.idiomatic: If the old ways had been adequate, peace would already have been achieved — why would it still weigh on my mind?"

sentences.zh: 因召恕等責以職事曠廢。

translations.literal: He thereupon summoned Shu and the others and rebuked them for neglect of duty.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Shu and the others and rebuked them for neglecting their duties.

sentences.zh: 恕等對曰：「今土宇至廣，庶務至繁，國用軍須，所費浩瀚，又遇諸州凡有災沴，必盡蠲其租。

translations.literal: Shu and the others replied: "Today the territory is extremely broad and ordinary affairs extremely complex. State expenditures and military needs cost vast sums. Moreover whenever any prefecture suffers disaster or pestilence, its taxes are fully remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and the others replied, "Today the realm is vast and ordinary affairs are endlessly complex. State expenditures and military needs cost enormous sums. Moreover, whenever any prefecture suffers disaster or pestilence, its taxes are fully remitted.

sentences.zh: 臣等每舉榷利，朝廷必以侵民為慮，皆尼而不行。

translations.literal: Whenever we propose monopolies and profits, the court invariably considers encroachment upon the people and blocks them from implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever we propose revenue monopolies, the court invariably fears they will encroach on the people and blocks them from being carried out.

sentences.zh: 縱使耿壽昌、桑弘羊復生，亦所不逮。

translations.literal: Even if Geng Shouchang and Sang Hongyang were reborn, they could not match the task.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Geng Shouchang and Sang Hongyang were reborn, they could not meet such demands.

sentences.zh: 臣等駑力，惟盡心簿領，終不足上裨聖治。」

translations.literal: We are feeble in strength and can only devote ourselves wholeheartedly to ledgers and accounts — in the end we are insufficient to benefit sage governance above."
translations.idiomatic: We are feeble in ability and can only devote ourselves wholeheartedly to the ledgers — in the end we are insufficient to aid your sage governance."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「卿等清而不通，專守繩墨，終不能為國家度長絜大，剖煩析滯。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "You are pure but not flexible, clinging single-mindedly to the rule book — in the end you cannot measure long and short or cut through complexity and stagnation for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "You are upright but inflexible, clinging rigidly to the rule book. In the end you cannot weigh large against small for the state or cut through complexity and stagnation.

sentences.zh: 只如京城倉庫，主吏當改職者，簿領中壹處節目未備，即至十年五年不決，以致貧無資給，轉徙溝壑。

translations.literal: Take only the capital's granaries and storehouses: when chief clerks should be transferred to new posts, if even one item in the accounts is incomplete they wait ten or five years without decision, until the clerks are poor with no resources and drift into gutters and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Take the capital's granaries and storehouses: when chief clerks due for transfer find even one item incomplete in the accounts, decisions are delayed five or ten years, until the clerks are destitute and die in ditches and ravines.

sentences.zh: 此卿等之過，豈不傷和氣哉？」

translations.literal: This is your fault — does it not harm harmony?"
translations.idiomatic: This is your fault — does it not destroy goodwill?"

sentences.zh: 恕等頓首謝。

translations.literal: Shu and the others kowtowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and the others kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 五年，賜三司錢百萬，募吏有能言本司不便者，令恕等量事大小，以錢賞之，錢盡更給。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, one million cash from the Three Directorates was granted to recruit clerks who could speak to inconveniences within their office. Shu and others were to measure the size of each matter and reward with cash; when funds were exhausted more would be provided.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year one million cash from the Three Directorates was granted to recruit clerks who could identify inconveniences within their offices. Shu and others were to measure the importance of each matter and reward them with cash; when the funds were exhausted more would be supplied.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，欲倂三司，命官總判。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, there was a plan to merge the Three Directorates and have one official supervise them overall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao there was a plan to merge the Three Directorates under a single supervising official.

sentences.zh: 其勾院、磨勘、理欠、憑由、支收、行帳、提點等司，令恕條列其事以聞。

translations.literal: The Audit Office, Review Office, Arrears Office, Voucher Office, Disbursement Office, Transit Account Office, and Inspection Office — Shu was ordered to itemize their affairs and report.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was ordered to itemize the affairs of the Audit Office, Review Office, Arrears Office, Voucher Office, Disbursement Office, Transit Account Office, and Inspection Office and report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 恕奏曰：「伏以封域寖廣，財穀繁多，三司之中，簿牒填委，朝廷設法，督責尤嚴，官吏救過不暇。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized: "I respectfully consider that the domain grows ever wider and revenues ever more abundant. Within the Three Directorates documents pile high. The court establishes methods with especially strict supervision and enforcement, and officials scarcely have time to remedy errors.
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized, "I respectfully observe that the realm grows ever wider and revenues ever more abundant. Within the Three Directorates documents pile high. The court sets rules with especially strict supervision, and officials scarcely have time to remedy their errors.

sentences.zh: 若為三部各設主司，擇才非難，辦事亦易。

translations.literal: If three departments each had a chief office and talented men were selected, that would not be difficult and administration would also be easier.
translations.idiomatic: If three departments each had a chief office and capable men were selected, that would not be difficult and administration would also be easier.

sentences.zh: 事辦過鮮，不撓上心，此亦一時之良策也。

translations.literal: When affairs were handled too lightly they would not disturb the imperial mind — this too would be a good policy for the time.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were handled promptly they would not trouble the imperial mind — this too would be a sound policy for the moment.

sentences.zh: 其勾院、磨勘兩司，出於舊制，關防之要，莫加於此。

translations.literal: The Audit Office and Review Office derive from the old system; for safeguarding control nothing surpasses them.
translations.idiomatic: The Audit Office and Review Office derive from the old system; for safeguarding and control nothing surpasses them.

sentences.zh: 理欠、憑由二司，雖非舊設，自理欠失序，憑由散落，故設二司專令典掌。

translations.literal: The Arrears Office and Voucher Office, though not old establishments, were set up because arrears fell out of order and vouchers were scattered — therefore two offices were specially established for dedicated custody.
translations.idiomatic: The Arrears Office and Voucher Office, though not old establishments, were created because arrears had fallen out of order and vouchers were scattered; therefore two offices were specially established to keep them in custody.

sentences.zh: 綱目咸具，制置有倫，逋欠無失理之名，憑由鮮流散之弊，實亦要切，不可廢除。

translations.literal: Categories and headings are all complete and the arrangement has logic; no arrears lack proper disposition, and few are the ills of scattered vouchers — this is truly essential and cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Categories and headings are complete and the arrangement is orderly; arrears need not go unsettled and vouchers need not scatter — this is truly essential and cannot be abolished.

sentences.zh: 若兩司並委一官，方及判官一員之事。

translations.literal: If both offices were entrusted to one official, it would barely amount to the work of a single adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: If both offices were entrusted to one official, the workload would barely equal that of a single adjutant.

sentences.zh: 其主轄支收司，先因從京支度財貨，轉輸外地，此除彼附，照驗稽滯，若京城得賢主史，使居此司，專行檢轄，凡支撥官物，便給除破文憑，卻於所司置簿記錄，催到收附文記，即乃勾銷簿書取捷之門，亦為允當。

translations.literal: As for the chief Disbursement Office: it originally arose because goods and funds were disbursed from the capital and transported to outer regions — verifying receipts here and delays there. If the capital obtains a capable chief clerk and assigns him to this office to conduct exclusive inspection and control, then whenever official goods are disbursed, disbursement vouchers can be issued on the spot; records are kept at the responsible office; when receipt documents are obtained and filed, ledger entries can then be written off — a shortcut gate that is also appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: As for the chief Disbursement Office, it originally arose because funds and goods were disbursed from the capital and transported to outer regions, with verification of receipts here and delays there. If the capital could place a capable chief clerk in this office to conduct exclusive inspection, then whenever official goods were disbursed, disbursement vouchers could be issued on the spot, records kept at the responsible office, and once receipt documents were obtained and filed the ledgers could be written off at once — a shortcut that would also be appropriate.

sentences.zh: 其行帳司近日權置，了絕舊帳，帳目告盡，司額自除。

translations.literal: The Transit Account Office was recently established on a provisional basis; once old accounts are cleared and the ledgers exhausted, the office establishment will naturally be removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Transit Account Office was recently established on a provisional basis. Once the old accounts are cleared and the ledgers exhausted, the office itself can naturally be abolished.

sentences.zh: 提點司是中旨特置，提振三司廢怠之事，固非有司敢得擬議也。」

translations.literal: The Inspection Office was specially established by imperial order to rouse laxity within the Three Directorates — this is indeed not something regular offices would dare propose."
translations.idiomatic: The Inspection Office was specially established by imperial order to rouse laxity within the Three Directorates — this is indeed not something regular offices would dare propose on their own."

sentences.zh: 詔三司都憑由、理欠司宜令為一處，命官兼判。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Central Voucher Office and Arrears Office of the Three Directorates merged into one location with an appointed official concurrently overseeing it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Central Voucher Office and Arrears Office of the Three Directorates combined into one location under an appointed official with concurrent oversight.

sentences.zh: 應諸道逋負官物，令三司逐部理約，理欠司但總其所逋之數糾督之。

translations.literal: For official goods owed on every circuit, the Three Directorates were to settle by department; the Arrears Office would only aggregate the total owed and supervise recovery.
translations.idiomatic: For official goods owed on every circuit, the Three Directorates were to settle accounts by department, while the Arrears Office would only aggregate the totals owed and supervise recovery.

sentences.zh: 餘悉從恕奏。

translations.literal: Everything else followed Shu's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else was adopted as Shu had proposed.

sentences.zh: 恕將立茶法，召茶商數十人，俾各條利害，恕閱之第為三等，語副使宋大初曰：「吾觀下等固滅裂無取。

translations.literal: When Shu was about to establish tea regulations, he summoned several dozen tea merchants and had each list advantages and disadvantages. After reading them Shu ranked them into three grades and said to Vice Commissioner Song Dachu: "I see the lowest grade is indeed fragmented and worthless.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was about to establish tea regulations, he summoned several dozen tea merchants and had each list the advantages and disadvantages. After reading them he ranked the proposals into three grades and said to Vice Commissioner Song Dachu, "The lowest grade is plainly fragmented and worthless.
