sentences.zh: 上等取利太深，此可行於商賈，不可行於朝廷。

translations.literal: The highest grade takes profit too deep — this may work for merchants but cannot work for the court.
translations.idiomatic: The highest grade seeks profit too aggressively — that may work for merchants but cannot work for the court.

sentences.zh: 惟中等公私皆濟，吾裁損之，可以經久。」

translations.literal: Only the middle grade benefits both public and private. If I trim and reduce it, it can last long."
translations.idiomatic: Only the middle grade serves both public and private interests. If I trim and adjust it, it can endure."

sentences.zh: 於是始為三法行之，貨財流通。

translations.literal: Thereupon he first implemented the three-method system and goods and cash circulated freely.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he first implemented the three-method system, and goods and cash circulated freely.

sentences.zh: 峽路諸州，承孟氏舊政，賦稅輕重不均，閬州稅錢千八百為一絹，果州六百為一絹。

translations.literal: The various prefectures of the Gorges route still followed the old policies of the Meng clan; tax burdens were uneven. Langzhou required 1,800 cash in tax for one bolt of silk; Guozhou, 600 for one bolt.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures of the Gorges route still followed the old policies of the Meng regime, and tax burdens were uneven: Langzhou required 1,800 cash in tax for one bolt of silk, while Guozhou required only 600.

sentences.zh: 民前後擊登聞鼓陳訴歷二十年，詔下本道官吏，因循不理。

translations.literal: The people repeatedly beat the Drum of Direct Appeal to state their grievances over twenty years. Edicts were sent down to the circuit officials, but they dragged their feet and did not handle the cases.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years the people had repeatedly beaten the Drum of Direct Appeal to air their grievances, yet though edicts went out to the circuit officials, they procrastinated and did nothing.

sentences.zh: 轉運副使張曄年少氣銳，會受詔按覆，即便宜行之。

translations.literal: Transport Vice Commissioner Zhang Ye was young and bold in spirit. When he happened to receive an edict to investigate and review the matter, he immediately acted at his discretion to implement reforms.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Vice Commissioner Zhang Ye was young and spirited. When he received an edict to investigate the matter, he immediately set about correcting it on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 恕奏曄擅改法，計果州一歲虧上供絹萬餘，曄坐削一任免。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized that Zhang Ye had changed the law on his own authority, calculating that Guozhou in one year fell short by more than ten thousand bolts in tribute silk to the court. Zhang Ye was punished by reduction of one rank and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Shu reported that Zhang Ye had altered the law without authorization, calculating that Guozhou's tribute silk to the court had fallen short by more than ten thousand bolts in a single year. Zhang Ye was demoted one rank and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 恕每便殿奏事，太宗或未深察，必形誚讓。

translations.literal: Whenever Shu reported matters in the informal audience hall, if Taizong had not thoroughly examined a matter, rebuke and reprimand would invariably appear on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shu reported matters in the informal audience hall, Taizong would openly rebuke him if he had not looked into something closely enough.

sentences.zh: 恕斂板踧縮，退至殿壁負立，若無所容。

translations.literal: Shu would close his memorial board and shrink back; withdrawing to the palace wall he would stand with his back against it, as if with nowhere to fit.
translations.idiomatic: Shu would fold his memorial board and shrink back, retreating to stand with his back against the palace wall as though there were nowhere he could hide.

sentences.zh: 俟意稍解復進，愨執前奏，終不改易，如是或至三四。

translations.literal: Waiting until the emperor's mood slightly eased he would advance again, steadfastly holding to his earlier memorial and never changing it — sometimes this would repeat three or four times.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's mood softened he would step forward again, holding firm to his original memorial without wavering — sometimes three or four times over.

sentences.zh: 太宗以其忠，多從之。

translations.literal: Taizong, because of his loyalty, often followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, valuing his loyalty, often accepted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加戶部，命條具中外錢穀以聞。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, he was additionally made Vice Minister of Revenue and ordered to itemize and report domestic and foreign cash and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong came to the throne, Shu was also given the title of Vice Minister of Revenue and ordered to compile detailed accounts of state revenues and grain stores throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 恕久不進，屢趣之，恕曰：「陛下富於春秋，若知府庫充實，恐生侈心，臣是以不敢進。」

translations.literal: Shu long did not submit the report. He was repeatedly urged. Shu said: "Your Majesty is in the prime of youth. If you knew how full the treasuries were, I fear you would develop extravagant impulses. Therefore your subject dares not submit it."
translations.idiomatic: Shu long delayed submitting the report, and when pressed repeatedly he said, "Your Majesty is still young. If you learned how full the treasuries truly are, you might grow extravagant in your tastes — that is why I have not dared to submit the accounts."

sentences.zh: 真宗嘉之。

translations.literal: Zhenzong praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong commended him for this.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，帝北巡，充行在轉運使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, when the emperor toured north, he served as transport commissioner in the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In 999, when the emperor toured the north, Shu served as transport commissioner for the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 俄以母老求解，拜吏部侍郎，知通進銀臺封駁司、審官院。

translations.literal: Soon, because his mother was aged, he requested leave and was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, concurrently directing the Directorate for Memorial Submission, the Silver Terrace Office for Memorial Review and Rejection, and the Bureau for the Review of Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, citing his aged mother, he requested leave and was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, with concurrent charge of the Directorate for Memorial Submission, the Silver Terrace Office for Memorial Review, and the Bureau for the Review of Officials.

sentences.zh: 上言：「封駁之任，實給事中之職，隸於左曹。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "The duty of memorial review and rejection is in truth the office of the Supervising Secretary, subordinate to the Left Office.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial arguing that "the duty of reviewing and rejecting memorials is properly that of the Supervising Secretary, subordinate to the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 雖別建官局，不可失其故號。

translations.literal: Although a separate bureau was established, its old designation must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Even though a separate bureau had been created, its original designation should not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 請以門下封駁事隸銀臺司。」

translations.literal: He requested that matters of review and rejection under the Secretariat be subordinated to the Silver Terrace Office."
translations.idiomatic: He requested that the Secretariat's duties of reviewing and rejecting memorials be placed under the Silver Terrace Office."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he supervised the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianping, he served as chief examiner for the metropolitan civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 恕自以洪人避嫌，凡江南貢士悉被黜退。

translations.literal: Shu, being himself a man of Hongzhou, avoided suspicion and rejected all candidates from Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: As a native of Hongzhou, Shu sought to avoid favoritism and disqualified every candidate from the Jiangnan region.

sentences.zh: 又援貢舉非其人之條，故所取甚少，而所取以王曾為首，及廷試糊名考校，曾復得甲科，時議稱之。

translations.literal: He also invoked the regulation against selecting unworthy candidates, so those he chose were very few. Among those chosen Wang Zeng ranked first. When the palace examination was conducted with names concealed for grading, Zeng again earned the top grade, and contemporary opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Invoking the regulation against selecting unworthy candidates, he chose very few — but chief among them was Wang Zeng, who again earned the top grade when names were concealed for the palace examination. Contemporary opinion praised Shu's judgment.

sentences.zh: 恕每自歎曰：「吾得曾，名世才也，不愧於知人矣。」

translations.literal: Shu would often sigh to himself: "In obtaining Zeng — a talent for the age — I am not ashamed of knowing men."
translations.idiomatic: Shu would often say with satisfaction, "In finding Zeng — a talent for the age — I have proved myself no poor judge of men."

sentences.zh: 恕事母孝，母亡，哀慕過甚，不食葷茹，遂至羸瘠。

translations.literal: Shu served his mother filially. When his mother died, his grief and longing were excessive. He ate no meat or vegetables with strong flavor and became emaciated.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was deeply filial toward his mother. After her death his grief was so intense that he abstained from meat and pungent foods until he grew gaunt and frail.

sentences.zh: 起復視事，遷尚書左丞、權知開封府。

translations.literal: Called back from mourning to resume office, he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning to resume duty, he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and made acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 恕已病，猶勉強親職，數月增劇，表求館殿之職，獲奉以濟其貧。

translations.literal: Shu was already ill, yet still forced himself to attend to his duties in person. After several months his condition worsened. He memorialized requesting a post in the Academy Hall, hoping to receive salary to relieve his poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Though already ill, Shu still forced himself to attend to his duties. When his condition worsened after several months, he requested an Academy post whose salary might ease his poverty.

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「卿求一人可代者，聽卿去。」

translations.literal: Zhenzong said: "If you recommend one person who can replace you, you may leave."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong said, "Recommend someone who can take your place, and you may be relieved."

sentences.zh: 是時寇準罷樞密使，恕即薦以自代，遂以準為三司使，恕為集賢學士、判院事。

translations.literal: At this time Kou Zhun had been removed as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Shu immediately recommended him as his replacement. Thereupon Kou Zhun was made Commissioner of the Three Departments, and Shu became Academician of the Collection of Eminent Writings and concurrent director of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun had just been removed as Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Shu immediately recommended him as his successor. Kou Zhun became Commissioner of the Three Departments, while Shu took the post of Academician of the Collection of Eminent Writings and director of the Academy.

sentences.zh: 準即檢尋恕前後改革興立之事，類以為冊，及以所出榜，別用新板，躬至恕第請判押。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun immediately searched out Shu's reforms and establishments from before and after, classified them into a register, and with the proclamations he had issued used new printing blocks; he went in person to Shu's residence to request his seal and signature.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun gathered all of Shu's past reforms and establishments into a compiled register, reprinted the proclamations on new blocks, and went in person to Shu's home to request his seal and signature.

sentences.zh: 恕亦不讓，一一押之，自是計使無不循其舊貫。

translations.literal: Shu also did not demur and affixed his seal to each one. From this point none of the commissioners of finance failed to follow his former practices.
translations.idiomatic: Shu did not hesitate but affixed his seal to each document. Thereafter every finance commissioner adhered to his established practices.

sentences.zh: 至李諮為三司使，始改茶法，恕之規模漸革矣。

translations.literal: Only when Li Zi became Commissioner of the Three Departments did the tea law begin to change, and Shu's system was gradually altered.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Li Zi became Commissioner of the Three Departments was the tea law changed, and Shu's framework was gradually dismantled.

sentences.zh: 帝重恕，詔太醫診療。

translations.literal: The emperor valued Shu and ordered imperial physicians to diagnose and treat him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, holding Shu in high regard, ordered imperial physicians to attend him.

sentences.zh: 百日，有司請停奉，不許，未幾，卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: At the hundredth day of mourning, the relevant offices requested that his salary be stopped. This was not permitted. Before long he died, at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: At the hundred-day mark of mourning, officials moved to halt his salary, but the emperor refused. Before long Shu died, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 恕將卒，口占遺奏及約束後事，送終之具，無不周悉。

translations.literal: As Shu was about to die, he orally dictated his final memorial and instructions for later matters; the provisions for his funeral — nothing was not thoroughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: As death approached, Shu dictated his final memorial and instructions for his affairs; every detail of his funeral arrangements was accounted for.

sentences.zh: 真宗悼惜，廢朝，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Zhenzong mourned and lamented him, cancelled court for a day, and posthumously conferred upon him the title of Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong grieved deeply, cancelled court for a day, and posthumously conferred on him the title of Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 錄其子執中為太常寺太祝，執古為奉禮郎。

translations.literal: His son Bozhong was enrolled as a Director of Ritual Music in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Zhigu as a Master of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bozhong was granted the post of Director of Ritual Music in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Zhigu was made a Master of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 恕頗涉史傳，多識典故，精於吏理，深刻少恩，人不敢干以私。

translations.literal: Shu read widely in historical works, knew many precedents and allusions, was skilled in administrative principles, was severe and sparing in grace; people did not dare to importune him with private requests.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was well versed in historical works and precedents, skilled in administrative affairs, stern and sparing in mercy — no one dared approach him with private requests.

sentences.zh: 前後掌利柄十餘年，強力幹事，胥吏畏服，有稱職之譽。

translations.literal: For more than ten years he successively held financial power. Forceful and effective in affairs, clerks feared and obeyed him, and he had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Having held the reins of finance for more than a decade, he was forceful and effective; clerks feared and obeyed him, and he enjoyed a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 善談論，聽者忘倦。

translations.literal: He was skilled in discourse; listeners forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He was an engaging speaker; listeners lost track of time.

sentences.zh: 素不喜釋氏，嘗請廢譯經院，辭甚激切，真宗曰：「三教之興，其來已久，前代毀之者多矣，但存而不論可也。」

translations.literal: He had never liked Buddhism. He once requested abolition of the Scripture Translation Institute, his language very vehement. Zhenzong said: "The rise of the Three Teachings has been long. Many in previous ages sought to destroy them. It is enough to keep them and not discuss them."
translations.idiomatic: He had always disliked Buddhism and once petitioned to abolish the Scripture Translation Institute in vehement terms. Zhenzong replied, "The Three Teachings have flourished for a very long time; many rulers before us tried to suppress them. It is enough simply to leave them be."

sentences.zh: 恕性吝，怒子淳私用錢。

translations.literal: Shu was by nature stingy and angry that his son Chun had used money privately.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was stingy by nature and furious that his son Chun had spent money without permission.

sentences.zh: 及寢疾，上言淳不率教導，多與非類遊，常習武藝，願出為外州軍校。

translations.literal: When he fell ill in bed, he memorialized that Chun did not obey instruction, associated much with unworthy company, and often practiced martial arts; he wished to have him sent out as a military officer in an outer prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, he reported that Chun was undisciplined, consorted with unsavory company, and trained constantly in martial arts — and asked that he be sent out as a military officer in a remote prefecture.

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「戎校管鎮兵，非丞郎家子弟所蒞也。」

translations.literal: Zhenzong said: "Command of frontier garrison troops is not a post for the sons of vice-ministerial families to hold."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong said, "Command of frontier garrison troops is no place for the son of a vice-ministerial family."

sentences.zh: 以為滁州司馬。

translations.literal: He was instead made Marshal of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Instead, Chun was made Marshal of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 恕卒，召復舊官，後竟以賄敗。

translations.literal: When Shu died, Chun was recalled to his former post, but in the end fell because of bribery.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu's death, Chun was recalled to his former post but was eventually ruined by a bribery scandal.

sentences.zh: 執中至同中書門下平章事，別有傳；

translations.literal: Bozhong rose to Grand Councilor of the Joint Secretariat and Chancellery; there is a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhong rose to serve as Grand Councilor; his biography appears elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 執古至虞部員外郎；

translations.literal: Zhigu reached the office of Vice Director in the Bureau of Parks and Forests.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu rose to Vice Director in the Bureau of Parks and Forests.

sentences.zh: 執方、執禮，並太子中舍。

translations.literal: Zhifang and Zhili both became Junior Gentlemen in the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang and Zhili both served as Junior Gentlemen in the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 魏羽者，字垂天，歙州婺源人。

translations.literal: Wei Yu, styled Chuitian, was a native of Wuyuan in Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yu, styled Chuitian, was from Wuyuan in Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 少能屬文，上書李煜，署弘文館校書郎。

translations.literal: In youth he could compose literary pieces. He submitted a memorial to Li Yu and was appointed Proofreader in the Hall of Extended Culture.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he showed literary talent; he submitted a memorial to Li Yu and was appointed Proofreader in the Hall of Extended Culture.

sentences.zh: 時建當塗縣為雄遠軍，以羽為判官。

translations.literal: At the time Dangtu County was established as the Xiongyuan Army; Yu was made its administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Dangtu County was established as the Xiongyuan Army, Yu was appointed its administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 宋師渡江出其境，羽以城降，太祖擢為太子中舍，仍舊職。

translations.literal: When Song troops crossed the Yangzi and passed through his territory, Yu surrendered the city. Taizu promoted him to Junior Gentleman in the Crown Prince's Household, retaining his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Song troops crossed the Yangzi into his territory, Yu surrendered the city. Taizu promoted him to Junior Gentleman in the Crown Prince's Household while retaining his existing duties.

sentences.zh: 金陵平，入朝，出知興州。

translations.literal: When Jinling was pacified, he entered court and was sent out as prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinling fell, he came to court and was appointed prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，知棣州，改京兆府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he was prefect of Dizhou and was transferred to the Capital Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he governed Dizhou and was then transferred to the Capital Metropolitan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，受詔詣瀛州覆軍市租，得隱漏數萬計。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he received an edict to go to Yingzhou to review military market taxes and uncovered concealed omissions amounting to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was ordered to Yingzhou to audit military market taxes and uncovered concealed shortfalls amounting to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 因上言：「本州錄事參軍郭震十年未代；

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a memorial: "In this prefecture, Recording Secretary Guo Zhen has served ten years without rotation;
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted a memorial noting that "in this prefecture, Recording Secretary Guo Zhen had served ten years without rotation;

sentences.zh: 河間令崔能前任即墨，未滿歲遷秩。

translations.literal: Helian Magistrate Cui Neng, having previously served in Jimo, was transferred in rank before a full year had passed.
translations.idiomatic: yet Helian Magistrate Cui Neng, who had previously served in Jimo, was promoted before a full year had passed.

sentences.zh: 有司調選失平，疏遠何由聞達，請罪典司，以肅欺弊。」

translations.literal: The offices of personnel assignment are unbalanced; how can the remote ever make themselves heard? I request punishment of those in charge to rectify fraud and abuse."
translations.idiomatic: The personnel offices were assigning posts unfairly — how could the remote ever make themselves heard? He requested punishment of those responsible to root out fraud and abuse."

sentences.zh: 上賜詔褒諭。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed an edict commending and instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 覆命，遷太常博士、知宋州，又徙閬州，就改膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: Upon returning from his mission he was transferred to Doctor of the Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Songzhou; he was then moved to Langzhou and concurrently promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Foodstuffs.
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning from his mission he was promoted to Doctor of the Imperial Sacrifices and appointed prefect of Songzhou, then transferred to Langzhou and concurrently promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Foodstuffs.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，起復蒞事，入判大理寺。

translations.literal: When his father died he was recalled from mourning to resume office and entered to serve as vice-director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he was recalled from mourning to resume duty and appointed vice-director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 歷度支、戶部二判官，召拜本曹郎中。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice-director in the Revenue and Personnel bureaus and was summoned to be director of his bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as vice-director in the Revenue and Personnel bureaus and was summoned to become director of his bureau.

sentences.zh: 因上疏言三司職官頗眾，願省其半，可以責成，仍條列利病凡二十事。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a memorial stating that the offices of the Three Departments were quite numerous and he wished to cut them by half so responsibilities could be fixed; he also listed twenty items of advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial arguing that the Three Departments had too many officials and proposing to cut their number in half so that responsibilities could be fixed, listing twenty specific recommendations in all.

sentences.zh: 詔下有司詳議，皆以為便。

translations.literal: An edict was sent down to the relevant offices for detailed deliberation; all considered it beneficial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was sent to the relevant offices for review, and all agreed his proposals would be beneficial.

sentences.zh: 改鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice-director of Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of vice-director of Salt and Iron.

sentences.zh: 時北邊多警，朝議耕戰之術，以羽為河北東路營田副使，改兩浙轉運使，遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: At the time alarms were frequent on the northern frontier; court deliberated on farming-and-fighting methods. Yu was made Deputy Commissioner of Garrison Agriculture on the Hebei East Circuit, transferred to transport commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits, and promoted to Director in the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: With alarms frequent on the northern frontier, the court debated methods of combining farming and warfare. Yu was made Deputy Commissioner of Garrison Agriculture on the Hebei East Circuit, then transferred to transport commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits and promoted to Director in the Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，選為秘書少監，逾月，遷左諫議大夫，俄拜度支使，改鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he was selected as Vice Director of the Imperial Library; within a month he was transferred to Left Remonstrating Censor, and soon appointed Commissioner of Revenue and then Commissioner of Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chunhua era he was selected as Vice Director of the Imperial Library; within a month he was promoted to Left Remonstrating Censor, and soon after appointed Commissioner of Revenue and then Commissioner of Salt and Iron.

sentences.zh: 四年，倂三部為一司，以羽判三司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the three departments were merged into one commission and Yu was made concurrent director of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the three departments were merged into a single commission, and Yu was appointed to direct it.

sentences.zh: 先是，三司簿領堆積，吏緣為姦，雖嘗更立新制，未為適中。

translations.literal: Previously, documents of the Three Departments piled up and clerks exploited this for fraud; though new systems had been instituted, none had been quite right.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, paperwork at the Three Departments had piled up and clerks exploited the chaos for fraud; though new systems had been tried, none had worked well.

sentences.zh: 是冬，羽上言：「依唐制天下郡縣為十道，兩京為左右計，各署判官領之。」

translations.literal: That winter Yu submitted a memorial: "Following the Tang system, the empire's prefectures and counties were divided into ten circuits, with the two capitals forming the Left and Right Commissions, each headed by appointed vice-directors."
translations.idiomatic: That winter Yu submitted a memorial proposing that "under the Tang system the empire's prefectures and counties were divided into ten circuits, with the two capitals forming the Left and Right Commissions, each headed by appointed vice-directors."

sentences.zh: 制三司使二員，以羽為左計使，董儼為右計使，中分諸道以隸焉。

translations.literal: Two Commissioners of the Three Departments were established; Yu was made Left Commissioner and Dong Yan Right Commissioner, and the circuits were divided between them for subordination.
translations.idiomatic: Two Commissioners of the Three Departments were established — Yu as Left Commissioner and Dong Yan as Right Commissioner — with the circuits divided between them.

sentences.zh: 未久，以非便罷，守本官，出知滑州。

translations.literal: Before long, because it was inconvenient, this was abolished. He retained his original rank and was sent out as prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the arrangement was abolished as impractical. Yu retained his original rank and was sent out as prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，起復，加給事中，徙潭州，遣使諭旨。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning, additionally made Supervising Censor, transferred to Tanzhou; an envoy was dispatched to convey the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning, promoted to Supervising Censor, and transferred to Tanzhou; an envoy was dispatched to convey the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，遷工部侍郎，連徙杭、揚二州，召權知開封府。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works, successively moved to Hang and Yang prefectures, and summoned to serve as acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong came to the throne, Yu was promoted to Vice Minister of Works, transferred in succession to Hangzhou and Yangzhou, and summoned to serve as acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 車駕北巡，判留司三司，再為戶部度支使。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured north, he concurrently directed the Three Departments in the capital during the emperor's absence and again served as Commissioner of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the north, Yu directed the Three Departments in the capital during his absence and again served as Commissioner of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，以疾解職，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping, citing illness he resigned office and was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1001, citing illness he resigned his post and was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 謝日，召升便殿，從容問諭，勉以醫藥。

translations.literal: On the day of his audience of thanks he was summoned to the informal hall; the emperor spoke with him at ease, inquiring and instructing him, and urged him to seek medical treatment.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his audience of thanks he was summoned to the informal hall, where the emperor spoke with him warmly, inquired after his health, and urged him to seek medical care.

sentences.zh: 月餘卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month he died, at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he died, at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 羽涉獵史傳，好言事。

translations.literal: Yu read widely in historical works and liked to speak on affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Yu read widely in historical works and was fond of speaking out on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，許王暴薨，或有以宮府舊事上聞者。

translations.literal: During Chunhua, Prince Xu died suddenly; someone reported old matters of the palace establishment to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era, Prince Xu died suddenly, and someone reported old affairs of the princely household to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，追捕僚吏，將窮究之。

translations.literal: Taizong was enraged, pursued and arrested the staff officers, and intended to investigate thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was enraged, ordered the arrest of the princely staff, and intended to investigate the matter to the full.

sentences.zh: 羽乘間上言曰：「漢戾太子竊弄父兵，當時言者以其罪當笞耳。

translations.literal: Yu seized an opening to submit a memorial: "When the Han Crown Prince Li privately wielded his father's troops, those who spoke at the time held his offense deserved only flogging.
translations.idiomatic: Yu seized an opportunity to submit a memorial: "When the Han Crown Prince Li privately wielded his father's troops, those who spoke at the time held that his offense deserved no more than flogging.

sentences.zh: 今許王之過，未甚於是。」

translations.literal: Prince Xu's fault today is not greater than this."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xu's fault today is no greater than that."

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉納之，繇是被劾者皆獲輕典。

translations.literal: Taizong gladly accepted this; thus those who had been impeached all received lighter punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong gladly accepted this counsel, and those who had been impeached all received lighter sentences.

sentences.zh: 嘗建議有唐以來，凡制詔皆經門下省審，有非便者許其封駁，請遵故事，擇名臣專領其職，迄今不廢。

translations.literal: He once proposed that since the Tang, all edicts and proclamations had been reviewed by the Secretariat, and if inconvenient they could be sealed and rejected; he requested following this precedent and selecting eminent ministers to specialize in the duty — to this day it has not been abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He once proposed reviving the Tang practice whereby all edicts and proclamations were reviewed by the Secretariat and could be sealed and rejected if found unsuitable, recommending that eminent ministers be appointed to specialize in this duty — a practice that endures to this day.

sentences.zh: 羽強力有吏幹，尤小心謹事。

translations.literal: Yu was forceful and had administrative skill, especially cautious and conscientious in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was forceful and capable in administration, especially cautious and conscientious in his duties.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗謂左右曰：「羽有心計，亦明吏道，但無執守，與物推移耳。

translations.literal: Taizong once said to those around him: "Yu is resourceful and understands administrative ways, but he has no fixed principles — he shifts with circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once remarked to those around him, "Yu is shrewd and understands the ways of administration, but he has no fixed principles — he simply shifts with circumstances.

sentences.zh: 歷劇職十年，始逾四十，鬚鬢盡白，亦可憐也。」

translations.literal: He held arduous posts for ten years, having just passed forty, and his beard and temples were entirely white — pitiable indeed."
translations.idiomatic: He held arduous posts for ten years, and though he had only just passed forty, his beard and temples had turned entirely white — a pitiable sight indeed."

sentences.zh: 羽出入計司凡十八年，習知金穀之事，然頗傷煩急，不達大體。

translations.literal: Yu went in and out of the finance commissions for eighteen years altogether, thoroughly knowing matters of cash and grain, yet he was somewhat excessively meticulous and did not grasp the larger picture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu spent eighteen years in all moving in and out of the finance commissions and knew the details of revenue and grain inside out, yet he was excessively meticulous and failed to grasp the larger picture.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，長子玠卒，其妻自陳家貧無祿，上憫之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, his eldest son Jie died; his wife reported that the family was poor and without salary; the emperor took pity.
translations.idiomatic: In 1005, his eldest son Jie died; when Jie's wife reported that the family was poor and without income, the emperor took pity on them.

sentences.zh: 次子校書郎瓘為奉禮郎，後為殿中丞；

translations.literal: His second son, Proofreader Guan, was made Master of Ceremonial and later Vice Director in the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Guan, a proofreader, was made Master of Ceremonial and later rose to Vice Director in the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 琰為太子中舍。

translations.literal: Yan was made Junior Gentleman in the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was made Junior Gentleman in the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 孫平仲，天禧三年同進士出身。

translations.literal: His grandson Pingzhong passed the metropolitan examination in the third year of Tianxi with the same-origin jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Pingzhong passed the metropolitan examination in 1019 with the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 羽同時有劉式者，亦久居計司，剏端拱中三年磨勘之法，首以式主之。

translations.literal: At the same time as Yu there was Liu Shi, who also long resided in the finance commissions; he created the three-year merit review method in the Duan Gong era, and Shi was first appointed to direct it.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary with Yu was Liu Shi, who also long served in the finance commissions; he devised the three-year merit review system in the Duan Gong era and was the first to direct it.

sentences.zh: 式，字叔度，袁州人也。

translations.literal: Shi, styled Shudu, was a man of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, styled Shudu, was from Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 李煜時，舉《三傳》中第。

translations.literal: During Li Yu's reign he passed the Classics of the Three Commentaries examination with honors.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Yu's reign he passed the examination in the Classics of the Three Commentaries with honors.

sentences.zh: 歸宋，歷遷大理寺丞、讚善大夫、監通州豐利監及主三司都磨勘司，仍賜緋。

translations.literal: After submitting to Song he was successively promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Grand Master of Exemplary Conduct, Supervisor of the Fengli Commissary in Tongzhou, and chief of the Three Departments Merit Review Office, and was also granted the scarlet robe.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting to the Song he rose through the ranks to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Grand Master of Exemplary Conduct, Supervisor of the Fengli Commissary in Tongzhou, and chief of the Three Departments Merit Review Office, and was granted the scarlet robe.

sentences.zh: 式又建議置主轄支收司，以謹財賦出納，時以為當。

translations.literal: Shi also proposed establishing a Directorate for Revenue Receipt and Disbursement to strictly manage fiscal receipts and payments; at the time this was considered appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Shi also proposed establishing a Directorate for Revenue Receipt and Disbursement to tighten control over fiscal receipts and payments, which was considered a sound measure at the time.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書丞，與陳靖使高麗。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and with Chen Jing served as envoy to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and served as envoy to Goryeo alongside Chen Jing.

sentences.zh: 至道中，倂三勾院為一，命式領之。

translations.literal: During the Zhidao era the three audit bureaus were merged into one and Shi was ordered to direct it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhidao era the three audit bureaus were merged into one, and Shi was appointed to direct it.

sentences.zh: 再轉工部員外郎，賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and granted the gold-and-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and granted the gold-and-purple insignia of high rank.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 式深究簿領之弊，江、淮間舊有橫賦，逋積至多，式奏免之，人以為便。

translations.literal: Shi thoroughly investigated abuses in ledger administration. Between the Yangzi and Huai there had long been unauthorized levies, and arrears had piled up to a great extent. Shi memorialized to have them abolished, and people regarded this as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Shi made a thorough study of abuses in fiscal record-keeping. Along the Yangzi and Huai rivers there had long been unauthorized surcharges, with enormous arrears accumulated over time. When Shi memorialized to have them abolished, people welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 然多所條奏，檢校過峻，為下吏所訟，免官，卒。

translations.literal: However, he submitted many separate memorials and his inspections were excessively severe; he was sued by his subordinates, was dismissed from office, and died.
translations.idiomatic: But he submitted memorial after memorial, and his inspections proved excessively harsh; subordinate officials brought charges against him, he was dismissed from office, and died.

sentences.zh: 真宗追錄前效，賜其子立本學究出身。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong posthumously recorded his earlier achievements and granted his son Liben an xuejiu jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong recognized his earlier service and granted his son Liben the xuejiu jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 次子立之，後為國子博士。

translations.literal: His second son Lizhi later became a Doctor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Lizhi later served as Doctor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 立德、立禮，並進士及第，立禮為殿中丞。

translations.literal: Lide and Lili both passed the metropolitan examination with highest honors; Lili became Vice Director in the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Lide and Lili both achieved jinshi status; Lili was appointed Vice Director in the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 劉昌言

translations.literal: Liu Changyan
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyan

sentences.zh: 劉昌言，字禹謨，泉州南安人。

translations.literal: Liu Changyan, styled Yumou, was a man of Nan'an in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyan, styled Yumou, was from Nan'an in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，文詞靡麗。

translations.literal: In his youth he was devoted to learning, and his literary compositions were ornate and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he applied himself devotedly to his studies, and his prose was elegant and florid.

sentences.zh: 本道節度陳洪進辟功曹參軍，掌箋奏。

translations.literal: The military commissioner of his circuit, Chen Hongjin, recruited him as Staff Adjutant and put him in charge of memorial drafts and submissions.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit military commissioner Chen Hongjin recruited him as Staff Adjutant, assigning him responsibility for memorial drafts.

sentences.zh: 洪進遣子文顯入貢，令昌言偕行，太祖親勞之。

translations.literal: Hongjin sent his son Wenxian to present tribute to the court and had Changyan accompany him; Emperor Taizu personally welcomed and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjin sent his son Wenxian to present tribute at court, he had Changyan accompany him; Emperor Taizu received them in person.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，洪進歸朝，改鎮徐州，又辟推官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, Hongjin submitted to the court; his post was changed to military commissioner of Xuzhou, and Changyan was again recruited as Administrative Aide.
translations.idiomatic: In 977, when Hongjin submitted to the Song court and was reassigned to Xuzhou, he again recruited Changyan as Administrative Aide.

sentences.zh: 五年，舉進士入格，太宗初惜科第，止授歸德軍掌書記。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered the jinshi examination and qualified; Emperor Taizong at first cherished the jinshi degree and would grant only the post of Secretary of the Guide Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 980 he passed the jinshi qualifying examination, but Emperor Taizong, still reluctant to grant full jinshi recognition, posted him only as secretary of the Guide Army command.

sentences.zh: 八年，復舉得第，遷保信、武信二鎮判官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he passed the examination again with honors and was transferred to be Administrative Judge of the Baoxin and Wuxin commands.
translations.idiomatic: In 983 he passed the examination with full honors and was appointed Administrative Judge at the Baoxin and Wuxin garrisons.

sentences.zh: 宰相趙普鎮南陽，重昌言有吏幹。

translations.literal: When the chief minister Zhao Pu was stationed at Nanyang, he valued Changyan's administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Minister Zhao Pu was posted at Nanyang, he greatly valued Changyan's administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 錢俶帥鄧，表薦之。

translations.literal: When Qian Chu commanded at Deng, he submitted a memorial recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Chu served as governor of Deng, he recommended Changyan by memorial.

sentences.zh: 移泰寧軍節度判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrative Judge under the Taining Army military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as Administrative Judge under the Taining Army commission.

sentences.zh: 入為左司諫、廣南安撫使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Left Remonstrating Censor and Pacification Commissioner for Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital as Left Remonstrating Censor and Pacification Commissioner for Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，趙普留守西京，表為通判，委以府政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chunhua era Zhao Pu remained as regent in the Western Capital; he submitted a memorial appointing Changyan as Vice Prefect and entrusted him with prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunhua era, when Zhao Pu served as regent in the Western Capital, he nominated Changyan as Vice Prefect and entrusted him with the administration of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 普疾，屬昌言後事。

translations.literal: When Pu fell ill, he entrusted his final affairs to Changyan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Pu fell ill, he entrusted his final affairs to Changyan.

sentences.zh: 普卒，昌言感普知己，經理其家事。

translations.literal: When Pu died, Changyan, moved by Pu's recognition of him, managed his household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Pu's death, Changyan, grateful for his patron's faith in him, took charge of his family's affairs.

sentences.zh: 太宗以為忠於所舉，拜起居郎，賜金紫、錢五十萬。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, considering him loyal to his patron's recommendation, appointed him Attendant-in-Ordinary and granted him gold-and-purple insignia and fifty thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, impressed by his loyalty to the man who had recommended him, appointed him Attendant-in-Ordinary and granted him the gold-and-purple insignia of high office together with fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 連對三日，皆至日旰。

translations.literal: For three days in succession he was summoned to audience, each lasting until sundown.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to audience three days running, each session lasting until sundown.

sentences.zh: 昌言捷給詼詭，能揣人主意，無不稱旨。

translations.literal: Changyan was quick-witted, nimble, and witty; he could discern what was in others' minds, and nothing he said failed to please the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and resourcefully witty, Changyan had a talent for reading others' intentions; nothing he said ever failed to please the emperor.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂宰相曰：「昌言質狀非偉，若以貌取，失之子羽矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to the chief ministers: "Changyan's physique and appearance are not imposing; if one judged by looks alone, one would have missed out on Ziyu."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong told the chief ministers: "Changyan is not imposing in stature; judge him by his appearance and you would have passed over Ziyu."

sentences.zh: 遷工部郎中，逾月，守本官，充樞密直學士，與錢若水同知審官院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Works; after more than a month, while retaining his original rank, he was appointed Hanlin Academician in the Privy Council, and together with Qian Ruoshui jointly directed the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works; a month later, while retaining that rank, he was made Hanlin Academician in the Privy Council and, together with Qian Ruoshui, directed the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 二十八日，遷右諫議大夫、同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day he was transferred to Right Remonstrating Grand Master and Deputy Commissioner of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth day he was promoted to Right Remonstrating Grand Master and Deputy Commissioner of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 昌言驟用，不為時望所伏，或短其閩語難曉，太宗曰：「惟朕能曉之。」

translations.literal: Changyan rose rapidly to office and was not admired by contemporary expectations; some criticized his Min dialect as hard to understand. Emperor Taizong said: "Only I can understand it."
translations.idiomatic: Changyan's rapid rise failed to win over the establishment; some complained that his Min dialect was hard to understand. "Only I can understand him," the emperor replied.

sentences.zh: 又短其委母妻鄉里，十餘年不迎侍，別娶旁妻。

translations.literal: Others also faulted him for leaving his mother and wife in his hometown, not bringing them to attend on him for more than ten years, and taking another wife on the side.
translations.idiomatic: Others faulted him for leaving his mother and wife in his hometown for more than ten years without bringing them to court, and for taking a concubine in the meantime.

sentences.zh: 太宗既寵之，詔令迎歸京師，本州給錢辦裝，縣次續食。

translations.literal: Since the emperor already favored him, an edict ordered him to bring his family back to the capital; his home prefecture was to provide money for travel expenses, and county relay stations were to supply successive meals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, still favoring him, ordered by edict that his family be brought to the capital; his home prefecture was to supply travel funds and relay stations along the route were to provide food.

sentences.zh: 時又有光祿丞何亮家果州，秘書丞陳靖家泉州，不迎其親。

translations.literal: At that time there were also Director of Ceremonials He Liang, whose family was in Guozhou, and Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Chen Jing, whose family was in Quanzhou; they too had not brought their parents to attend on them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Director of Ceremonials He Liang, from Guozhou, and the Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Chen Jing, from Quanzhou, likewise had failed to bring their parents to court.

sentences.zh: 下詔戒諭文武官，父母在劍南、峽路、漳泉、福建、嶺南，皆令迎侍，敢有違者，御史臺糾舉以聞。

translations.literal: An edict was issued warning civil and military officials: those whose parents were in Jiannan, the Gorges routes, Zhang-Quan, Fujian, or Lingnan were all ordered to bring them to attend on them; any who dared violate this would be impeached by the Censorate and reported.
translations.idiomatic: An edict warned civil and military officials throughout the empire that those whose parents lived in Jiannan, the Gorges routes, Zhang-Quan, Fujian, or Lingnan must bring them to court; violators would be impeached by the Censorate and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 昌言自以登擢非次，懼人傾奪。

translations.literal: Changyan, considering that his elevation was out of the usual order, feared that others would undermine and displace him.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan knew his promotion had been unusually rapid and lived in fear of being undermined by rivals.

sentences.zh: 會誅凶人趙讚，昌言與讚素善，前在河南嘗保任之，心不自安。

translations.literal: When the criminal Zhao Zan was executed, Changyan had long been on good terms with Zan and had previously vouched for him in Henan; he was ill at ease in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the notorious Zhao Zan was put to death, Changyan—who had long been friendly with him and had once vouched for him in Henan—was deeply unsettled.

sentences.zh: 因太宗言及近侍有與讚交者，昌言蹶然出位，頓首稱死罪。

translations.literal: When the emperor mentioned that some among the close attendants had associated with Zan, Changyan suddenly sprang from his place, prostrated himself, and declared himself guilty of a capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor remarked that some of his close attendants had consorted with Zan, Changyan suddenly leapt from his seat, prostrated himself, and confessed a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 太宗慰勉之，然自此惡其為人。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong comforted and encouraged him, but from then on came to dislike his character.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him, but from that day forward held his character in contempt.

sentences.zh: 以給事中罷，出知襄州。

translations.literal: He was dismissed as Supervising Censor and sent out to serve as prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Removed from office as Supervising Censor, he was posted as prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上言：「水旱民輸稅愆期。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial stating: "Because of floods and drought the people fell behind in paying taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Because of flood and drought the people have fallen behind on their tax payments.

sentences.zh: 舊制六月開倉，臣令先一月許所在縣驛輸納以便民。

translations.literal: The previous rule opened the granaries in the sixth month; I ordered that one month earlier the local counties and relay stations be permitted to collect and forward payments to ease the burden on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule granaries opened in the sixth month; I permitted collection to begin a month early at county stations and relay posts to ease the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 獲盜當部送闕下，臣恐吏柔懦不能制，再亡命，配隸軍籍。

translations.literal: Captured bandits were supposed to be escorted to the capital under guard; I feared that timid officials could not control them and they would escape again, so I assigned them to military registers instead.
translations.idiomatic: Captured bandits were to be escorted to the capital, but fearing that timid officials could not restrain them and they might escape again, I assigned repeat offenders to military service instead.

sentences.zh: 此二事，臣從便宜，不如詔書，慮讒慝因而浸潤，願陛下察之。」

translations.literal: In these two matters I acted for convenience and did not follow the edicts; I fear that slander and malice may gradually work their way in, and I beg Your Majesty to examine the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In both cases I acted expediently rather than strictly by edict; I fear that malicious slander may take hold, and I beg Your Majesty to look into it.

sentences.zh: 太宗下詔責其不循舊章，斂怨於民，自今敢背棄詔條，譴責不復恕。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong issued an edict reproaching him for not following established statutes and arousing popular resentment; from now on, whoever dared abandon the edict's provisions would be censured without further leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong issued an edict censuring him for departing from established rules and incurring popular resentment, and declared that henceforth anyone who defied imperial regulations would be punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，徙知荊南府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he was transferred to serve as prefect of Jingnan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 996 he was transferred to serve as prefect of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，就拜工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, Changyan was immediately appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, he was immediately appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，卒，年五十八，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he died at the age of fifty-eight and was posthumously granted the title Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 999 at the age of fifty-eight and was posthumously granted the title of Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 子有方，比部員外郎；

translations.literal: His son Youfang was Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youfang served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 有政，虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: Youzheng was Vice Director in the Ministry of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youzheng served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 張洎，滁州全椒人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji was a man of Quanjiao in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji was from Quanjiao in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖旼，澄城尉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Min was magistrate of Chengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Min served as magistrate of Chengcheng.

sentences.zh: 祖蘊，泗上轉運巡官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yun was Circuit Inspector for transport on the Si River.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yun served as transport circuit inspector on the Si River.

sentences.zh: 父煦，滁州司法掾。

translations.literal: His father Xu was a legal clerk in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu served as legal clerk in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 洎少有俊才，博通墳典。

translations.literal: Ji from youth had outstanding talent and broad mastery of the classics and archives.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ji showed exceptional talent and mastered the classics and historical archives.

sentences.zh: 江南舉進士，解褐上元尉。

translations.literal: In Jiangnan he passed the jinshi examination and upon leaving office robes became magistrate of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan he passed the jinshi examination and took up his first office as magistrate of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 李景長子弘冀卒，有司諡武宣，洎議以為世子之禮，但當問安視膳，不宜以「武」為稱，旋命改諡，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: When Li Jing's eldest son Hongji died, the relevant offices gave the posthumous title Wuxuan; Ji argued that the rites for a crown prince required only inquiring after his health and viewing his meals, and that "Wu" should not be used in the title; the title was promptly changed, and Ji was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing's eldest son Hongji died, the court proposed the posthumous title Wuxuan; Ji argued that a crown prince's rites called only for inquiring after his health and attending his meals, and that "Wu" was an inappropriate epithet. The title was promptly revised, and Ji was promoted to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 洎自以論事稱旨，遂肆彈擊無所忌，大臣遊簡言等嫉之。

translations.literal: Ji, considering that his policy recommendations pleased the emperor, then launched impeachments without restraint or fear; senior ministers such as You Jianyan envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Confident that his policy arguments pleased the emperor, Ji began impeaching officials without restraint; senior ministers including You Jianyan came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 會景遷國豫章，留煜居守，即薦洎為煜記室，不得從。

translations.literal: When Jing moved the capital to Yuzhang and left Yu to remain and guard it, he immediately recommended Ji as Yu's secretary, but Ji was not permitted to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing moved the capital to Yuzhang and left Li Yu to hold the fort, he recommended Ji as Li Yu's secretary—but Ji was not allowed to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，景卒，煜嗣。

translations.literal: Before long Jing died and Yu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Jing died and Li Yu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 擢工部員外郎、試知制誥；

translations.literal: Ji was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and provisionally appointed to draft imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and provisionally appointed to draft imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 滿歲，為禮部員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: After a full year he became Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites and Director of Edict Drafting.
translations.idiomatic: After one year he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites and Director of Edict Drafting.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人、清輝殿學士，參預機密，恩寵第一。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Drafting Secretary and Academician of the Qinghui Hall, participating in confidential matters; his favor was supreme.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Drafting Secretary and Academician of the Qinghui Hall, with a role in confidential state affairs; no one enjoyed greater favor at court.

sentences.zh: 洎舊字師黯，改字偕仁。

translations.literal: Ji formerly used the style Shi'an and changed it to Xieren.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had originally used the courtesy name Shi'an and changed it to Xieren.

sentences.zh: 清輝殿在後苑中，煜寵洎，不欲離左右，授職內殿，中外之務一以諮之。

translations.literal: The Qinghui Hall was in the inner gardens; Yu favored Ji and did not wish him to leave his side; he was given a post in the inner palace, and all internal and external affairs were entrusted entirely to his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The Qinghui Hall stood in the inner palace gardens; Li Yu so favored Ji that he kept him constantly at his side, gave him an inner-palace post, and consulted him on all matters domestic and foreign.

sentences.zh: 每兄弟宴飲，作妓樂，洎獨得預。

translations.literal: Whenever the brothers feasted and drank with musical entertainment, Ji alone was permitted to join.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet the royal brothers held with musical entertainment, Ji alone was invited to attend.

sentences.zh: 為建大第宮城東北隅，及賜書萬餘卷。

translations.literal: For him a great mansion was built in the northeast corner of the palace city, and more than ten thousand scrolls of books were granted.
translations.idiomatic: A grand mansion was built for him in the northeast corner of the palace city, and he was granted more than ten thousand scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 煜嘗至其第，召見妻子，賜予甚厚。

translations.literal: Yu once went to his mansion, summoned his wife and children to audience, and bestowed very generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu once visited his mansion, received his wife and children in audience, and lavished generous gifts upon them.

sentences.zh: 洎尤好建議，每上言，未即行，必稱疾，煜手劄慰諭之，始復視事。

translations.literal: Ji was especially fond of making proposals; whenever he submitted a recommendation that was not immediately implemented, he invariably pleaded illness; Yu would write him a personal letter of comfort and reassurance, and only then would he resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was fond of offering advice; whenever a proposal went unimplemented he would plead illness until Li Yu wrote him a personal letter of reassurance, whereupon he would return to duty.

sentences.zh: 及王師圍城，逾年，城危甚，洎勸煜勿降，每引符命云：「玄象無變，金湯之固，未易取也。

translations.literal: When the imperial army besieged the city, after more than a year the city was in grave peril; Ji urged Yu not to surrender, citing prognostications each time and saying: "The heavenly signs have not changed; the solidity of metal ramparts and moats of earth is not easily overcome.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song army besieged the city for more than a year and the situation grew desperate, Ji urged Li Yu not to surrender, citing omens each time: "The constellations have not shifted; our walls of bronze and moats of earth are not easily taken.

sentences.zh: 北軍旦夕當自引退。

translations.literal: The northern army will withdraw of its own accord before long.
translations.idiomatic: The northern army will withdraw on its own before long.

sentences.zh: 苟一旦不虞，即臣當先死。」

translations.literal: If some unforeseen disaster should come in a single day, then your servant will be the first to die."
translations.idiomatic: If the worst should befall us, I shall be the first to die."

sentences.zh: 既而城陷，洎攜妻子及橐裝，自便門入止宮中，紿光政使陳喬同升閣，欲與俱死。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell; Ji took his wife, children, and valuables, entered through the side gate and lodged in the palace, deceived Director of Brilliant Governance Chen Qiao into ascending the tower with him, intending to die together.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Ji took his wife, children, and valuables, entered the palace through a side gate, and tricked Director of Brilliant Governance Chen Qiao into joining him on the tower, intending that they die together.

sentences.zh: 喬自經氣絕，洎反下見煜曰：「臣與喬同掌樞務，國亡當俱死。

translations.literal: Qiao hanged himself and expired; Ji then descended and saw Yu, saying: "Your servant and Qiao together directed confidential affairs; when the state perishes we ought to die together.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao hanged himself and died; Ji then came down to see Li Yu and said: "Chen Qiao and I together managed affairs of state; when the realm falls we ought to die together.

sentences.zh: 又念主在，誰能為主白其事，不死，將有以報也。」

translations.literal: Yet considering that the sovereign remains, who could explain matters on the sovereign's behalf if I did not live? By not dying, I shall still have means to repay my debt."
translations.idiomatic: But with Your Majesty still alive, who would speak for you if I died? By living on, I may yet serve you."

sentences.zh: 歸朝，太祖召責之曰：「汝教煜不降，使至今日。」

translations.literal: After submitting to the court, Emperor Taizu summoned and rebuked him, saying: "You advised Yu not to surrender, bringing matters to what they are today."
translations.idiomatic: After the surrender, Emperor Taizu summoned and rebuked him: "You persuaded Li Yu not to capitulate and brought us to this day."

sentences.zh: 因出帛書示之，乃圍城日洎所草詔，召上江救兵蠟丸書也。

translations.literal: He then produced a silk document and showed it to him—it was the draft edict Ji had composed during the siege calling for rescue troops from upstream on the Yangzi, sealed in a wax pill.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then produced a silk document—the draft edict Ji had written during the siege, sealed in a wax pellet, summoning rescue forces from upstream on the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 洎頓首請罪曰：「實臣所為也。

translations.literal: Ji prostrated himself and pleaded guilty, saying: "It was indeed your servant who did this.
translations.idiomatic: Ji prostrated himself and confessed: "I did this.

sentences.zh: 犬吠非其主，此其一爾，他尚多有。

translations.literal: A dog barks not for its proper master—this is but one instance; there are many others besides.
translations.idiomatic: A dog barks not for its true master—this is but one example; there are many more.

sentences.zh: 今得死，臣之分也。」

translations.literal: Now to be allowed to die is your servant's proper portion."
translations.idiomatic: Death is what I deserve."

sentences.zh: 辭色不變。

translations.literal: His words and expression did not change.
translations.idiomatic: His expression never changed.

sentences.zh: 上奇之，貸其死，謂曰：「卿大有膽，不加卿罪。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at him, spared his life, and said: "You have great courage; I will not add to your offenses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by his composure, spared his life, and said: "You have remarkable courage; I will not punish you.

sentences.zh: 今之事我，無替昔日之忠也。」

translations.literal: In serving me now, do not fall short of the loyalty you showed in former days."
translations.idiomatic: Serve me now with the same loyalty you once showed your lord."

sentences.zh: 拜太子中允，歲餘，判刑部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Gentleman in the Crown Prince's Household; after more than a year he served as judge in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Junior Gentleman in the Crown Prince's Household and, after little more than a year, served as judge in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，以其文雅，選直舍人院，考試諸州進士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, on account of his refined literacy he was selected for the Drafting Academy and assigned to examine jinshi candidates from the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Ji was selected for the Drafting Academy on account of his literary cultivation and assigned to examine jinshi candidates from the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 未幾，使高麗，復命，改戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent as envoy to Goryeo; upon returning he was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he served as envoy to Goryeo, and upon his return was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，出知相州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo he was sent out to serve as prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 979 he was posted as prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，徙貝州。

translations.literal: The next summer he was transferred to Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer he was transferred to Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 是冬，又知相州。

translations.literal: That winter he again served as prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he returned to serve as prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 部內不治，轉運使田錫言其狀，代還。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction affairs were poorly administered; Transport Commissioner Tian Xi reported the situation, and he was replaced and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Within his jurisdiction governance was poor; Transport Commissioner Tian Xi reported this, and he was replaced and recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 洎求見廷辯，上以其儒生，不責以吏事，詔不問。

translations.literal: Ji requested an audience to dispute the matter in court; the emperor, considering him a scholar, did not hold him responsible for administrative matters and ordered that he not be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Ji requested an audience to defend himself before the throne; the emperor, treating him as a scholar rather than an administrator, ordered that no inquiry be made.

sentences.zh: 令以本官知譯經院，遷兵部員外郎、禮、戶二部郎中。

translations.literal: He was ordered to retain his original rank and direct the Sutra Translation Institute; he was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of War and then Director in the Ministries of Rites and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was directed to retain his rank while directing the Sutra Translation Institute, and was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War and then Director in the Ministries of Rites and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，同知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he jointly directed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 985 he served as co-director of the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，契丹寇邊，詔群臣言事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duan Gong era the Khitan raided the frontier; an edict ordered the officials to submit proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duan Gong era, when the Khitan raided the frontier, the emperor ordered officials throughout the court to submit policy recommendations.

sentences.zh: 洎上奏，以練兵聚穀，分屯塞下，來則備禦，去則勿追為要略。

translations.literal: Ji submitted a memorial proposing that the essential strategy was to drill troops and stock grain, garrison them separately below the passes, prepare defenses when the enemy came, and not pursue when they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Ji memorialized that the key strategy was to train troops, stockpile grain, and station garrisons below the frontier passes—holding firm when the enemy came and refusing pursuit when they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會錢俶薨，太常定諡忠懿。

translations.literal: When Qian Chu died, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices fixed his posthumous title as Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Chu died, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous title Zhongyi, "Loyal and Virtuous."

sentences.zh: 洎時判考功，為覆狀，經尚書省集議。

translations.literal: Ji was at the time serving as administrator of the Merit Review Office and drafted the review memorandum; it passed through collective deliberation at the Department and Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was then serving in the Merit Review Office and drafted the review memorandum, which went to the Ministry of Personnel for collective deliberation.

sentences.zh: 虞部郎中張佖奏駁曰：「按考功覆狀一句云『亢龍無悔』，實非臣子宜言者。

translations.literal: Director in the Ministry of Public Works Zhang Bi submitted a rebuttal, stating: "According to one phrase in the Merit Review memorandum, 'the dragon in exalted position without regret'—this is truly not language a subject should use.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bi, Director in the Ministry of Public Works, submitted an objection: "The review memorandum contains the phrase 'the dragon in exalted position without regret'—language no subject ought to use.

sentences.zh: 況錢俶生長島夷，夙為荒服，未嘗略居尊位，終是藩臣，故名不可稱龍，位不可為亢。

translations.literal: Moreover, Qian Chu grew up among the island barbarians and was long part of the wild frontier; he never even briefly occupied an exalted position and was ultimately only a frontier vassal—therefore the name 'dragon' cannot be applied to him, nor can the position be called 'exalted.'
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chu grew up among the island peoples of the wild frontier and never truly held supreme power; he remained a vassal lord to the end—'dragon' is not a fitting term for him, nor 'exalted position' for his rank.

sentences.zh: 其『亢龍無悔』四字，請改正。」

translations.literal: As for these four characters 'the dragon in exalted position without regret,' I request they be revised."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that these four characters be revised."

sentences.zh: 事下中書，以詰洎。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Secretariat to question Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was sent to the Secretariat to demand an explanation from Ji.

sentences.zh: 對狀曰：「竊以故秦國王明德茂勳，格於天壤，處崇高之富貴，絕纖介之譏嫌。

translations.literal: In his written response he stated: "I respectfully consider that the late Prince of Qin possessed brilliant virtue and abundant merit reaching to heaven and earth, occupying lofty wealth and honor, untainted by the slightest slander or reproach.
translations.idiomatic: In his written reply he argued: "The late Prince of Qin possessed brilliant virtue and abundant merit reaching heaven and earth; he enjoyed lofty wealth and honor untainted by the slightest reproach.

sentences.zh: 太常禮院稽其功行，定茲嘉諡，考功詳覆之際，率遵至公，故其議狀云：『茲所謂受寵若驚，居亢無悔者也』。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices examined his achievements and conduct and fixed this fine posthumous title; at the time the Merit Review Office conducted its detailed review, it wholly followed the utmost fairness, therefore its deliberation memorandum stated: 'This is what is meant by receiving favor as if startled, occupying an exalted position without regret.'
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices assessed his achievements and conduct and settled on this fine posthumous title; in its detailed review the Merit Review Office acted with complete impartiality, and therefore wrote: 'This is what is meant by receiving favor with trepidation and occupying an exalted position without regret.'

sentences.zh: 謹按《易·乾》之九三云：『君子乾乾，夕惕若厲，無咎。』

translations.literal: Respectfully citing the third line of Qian in the Book of Changes: 'The noble person is vigorous and vigilant; at evening he is wary as if in danger—there is no blame.'
translations.idiomatic: I cite the third line of Qian in the Book of Changes: 'The noble person works tirelessly and vigilantly; at evening he remains wary as if facing danger—and so incurs no blame.'

sentences.zh: 王弼注云：『處下體之極，居上體之下，履重剛之險，因時而惕，不失其幾，可以無咎。

translations.literal: Wang Bi's commentary states: 'Occupying the extremity of the lower trigram, situated below the upper trigram, treading the peril of doubled yang, alert according to the times, not missing the right moment—there can be no blame.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi's commentary reads: 'At the farthest reach of the lower trigram, yet still beneath the upper body, walking the danger of doubled yang—staying vigilant in season and never missing the crucial moment, one may incur no blame.'

sentences.zh: 處下卦之極，愈於上九之亢。』

translations.literal: Occupying the extremity of the lower trigram is better than the excess of the ninth line in the upper trigram.
translations.idiomatic: To stand at the limit of the lower trigram is still preferable to the overreach of the upper ninth line.

sentences.zh: 《易例》云：『初九為元士，九二為大夫，九三為諸侯。』

translations.literal: The Commentaries on the Changes state: 'The first nine line represents the chief officer, the second nine the grand master, the third nine the feudal lord.'
translations.idiomatic: The Commentaries on the Changes explain: 'Line one represents the chief officer, line two the grand master, line three the feudal lord.'

sentences.zh: 《正義》云：『《易》之本理，以體為君臣。

translations.literal: The Subcommentary states: 'The fundamental principle of the Changes uses the trigrams to represent ruler and minister.'
translations.idiomatic: The Subcommentary explains: 'The underlying logic of the Changes treats the trigrams as emblematic of the relationship between ruler and minister.'

sentences.zh: 九三居下體之極，是人臣之體也。

translations.literal: The third nine occupies the extremity of the lower trigram—it is the position of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Line three stands at the farthest point of the lower trigram—it represents the minister's station.

sentences.zh: 其免亢龍之咎者，是人臣之極，可以慎守免禍。

translations.literal: That it avoids the fault of the overreaching dragon is because it is the ultimate limit for a minister—through careful preservation one may avoid calamity.
translations.idiomatic: That it escapes the fault of the overreaching dragon is because it marks the utmost limit for a minister—through careful self-restraint one may avoid disaster.

sentences.zh: 故云免亢極之禍也。』

translations.literal: Therefore it is said that one avoids the calamity of overreach.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the text speaks of escaping the disaster of excessive elevation.

sentences.zh: 《漢書·梁商傳》贊云：『地居亢滿，而能以謹厚自終。』

translations.literal: The encomium in the Biography of Liang Shang in the Book of Han states: 'Though his position bordered on fullness, he was able through diligence and humility to see his life through to the end.'
translations.idiomatic: The encomium to Liang Shang in the Book of Han reads: 'Though his station verged on the pinnacle, he preserved himself through conscientious humility to the end of his days.'

sentences.zh: 楊植《許由碑》云：『錙銖九有，亢極一夫。』

translations.literal: Yang Zhi's Stele for Xu You states: 'The nine realms weighed in pin and ounce, yet one man stood at the apex.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi's Stele for Xu You declares: 'Though the realm itself weighed but trifles, one man stood at the summit of all.'

sentences.zh: 杜鴻漸《讓元帥表》云：『祿位亢極，過逾涯量。』

translations.literal: Du Hongjian's Petition Declining the Post of Marshal states: 'Rank and stipend at the apex, surpassing all measure.'
translations.idiomatic: In Du Hongjian's Petition Declining the Post of Marshal we read: 'Office and emolument at the very summit—far beyond what measure allows.'

sentences.zh: 盧杞《郭子儀碑》云：『居亢無悔，其心益降。』

translations.literal: Lu Qi's Stele for Guo Ziyi states: 'Occupying the apex without regret, his heart grew ever more humble.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi's Stele for Guo Ziyi says: 'Standing at the summit without remorse, he became only more humble in heart.'

sentences.zh: 李翰《書霍光傳》云：『有伊、周負荷之明，無九三亢極之悔。』

translations.literal: Li Han's Essay on the Biography of Huo Guang states: 'He possessed the luminous burden-bearing wisdom of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, without the regret of line three's overreach.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Han's Essay on the Biography of Huo Guang observes: 'He had the enlightened capacity to bear the realm that Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou possessed, without the remorse of line three's excessive elevation.'

sentences.zh: 張說《祁國公碑》云：『一無目牛之全，一無亢龍之悔也。』

translations.literal: Zhang Yue's Stele for the Duke of Qi states: 'One lacked the wholeness of the ox before his eyes; one lacked the regret of the overreaching dragon.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue's Stele for the Duke of Qi declares: 'The one lacked the full mastery of butchering an ox; the other lacked the remorse of the overreaching dragon.'

sentences.zh: 況考功狀內止稱云『受寵若驚，居亢無悔』，即本無『亢龍無悔』之語。

translations.literal: Moreover, within the Merit Review memorandum the text states only 'receiving favor as if startled, occupying the apex without regret'—there was originally no phrase 'the overreaching dragon without regret.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Merit Review memorandum spoke only of 'receiving favor with trepidation, occupying the apex without regret'—the phrase 'overreaching dragon without regret' appears nowhere in the original.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋張佖擅改公奏，罔冒天聰。

translations.literal: This must be Zhang Bi's unauthorized alteration of the public memorial, deceiving the imperial ear.
translations.idiomatic: This was surely Zhang Bi's unauthorized tampering with the official memorial—a fraud upon the imperial ear.

sentences.zh: 請以元狀看詳，反坐其人，以懲奸妄。」

translations.literal: I request that the original document be examined in detail and that he be punished by reversal of charge, to chastise such wicked presumption."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the original memorial be reviewed and the offender punished in turn, as a warning against such brazen deceit."

sentences.zh: 俄下詔曰：「張洎援引故實，皆有依據。

translations.literal: Shortly an edict was issued stating: 'Zhang Ji's citations of ancient precedents all have proper foundations.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward an edict declared: 'Zhang Ji's citations of historical precedent are all well grounded.

sentences.zh: 張佖學識甚淺，敷陳失實，尚示矜容，免其黜降，可罰一月俸。」

translations.literal: Zhang Bi's learning is very shallow and his presentation of the facts is erroneous; yet still he is shown indulgence—he is spared demotion and dismissal and is fined one month's salary."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bi's scholarship is shallow and his account of the facts inaccurate; nevertheless he is shown indulgence—spared dismissal but fined one month's salary."

sentences.zh: 洎未幾選為太僕少卿、同知京朝官考課，拜右諫議大夫、判大理寺。

translations.literal: Before long Ji was selected as Vice Director of the Imperial Stud and jointly directed the Merit Review of Metropolitan Officials; he was appointed Right Remonstrating Grand Master and put in charge of the Court of Judicial Review.
