translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Stud and co-director of metropolitan official merit review, then Right Remonstrating Grand Master with charge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 又充史館修撰、判集賢院事。

translations.literal: He also served as Historiographer in the History Institute and directed affairs of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as History Institute compiler and directed the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，上令史館修撰楊徽之等四人修正入閣舊圖，洎同奏詔，因討論故事，獨草奏以聞。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era the emperor ordered four History Institute compilers including Yang Huizhi to revise the old diagrams for entering the Inner Hall; Ji jointly received the edict to report, and in discussing precedents he alone drafted the memorial to submit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era the emperor ordered Yang Huizhi and three other History Institute compilers to revise the old protocol for entering the Inner Hall. Ji participated in the deliberations under imperial directive and alone drafted the memorial reporting their findings.

sentences.zh: 洎又言：

translations.literal: Ji also stated:
translations.idiomatic: Ji also submitted the following:

sentences.zh: 「按舊史，中書、門下、御史臺為三署，謂侍從供奉之官。

translations.literal: "According to the old histories, the Secretariat, Chancellery, and Censorate constituted the Three Offices—that is, the officials who attend and serve the throne.
translations.idiomatic: "According to older records, the Secretariat, Chancellery, and Censorate formed the Three Offices—the body of officials who attend upon and serve the throne.

sentences.zh: 今起居日侍從官先入殿庭，東西立定，俟正班入，一時起居。

translations.literal: Now on attendance days the attending officials enter the hall first, take their places east and west, wait for the full court to enter, and all perform attendance at once.
translations.idiomatic: Under the present practice, on attendance days the attending officials enter the hall first, stand east and west, and wait for the full court to enter before all performing attendance together.

sentences.zh: 其侍從官東西列拜，甚失北面朝謁之儀。

translations.literal: The attending officials bow in columns east and west—a grave violation of the rites of an audience facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The attending officials bow in separate east-west columns—a serious departure from the proper rites of a north-facing audience.

sentences.zh: 請準舊儀，侍從官先入起居，行畢，分侍立於丹墀之下，謂之『蛾眉班』。

translations.literal: I request that the old ritual be followed: attending officials enter first for attendance; when this is complete they divide and stand attendantly below the red steps—this is called the 'Moth-Eyebrow Formation.'
translations.idiomatic: I request a return to the old rite: attending officials enter first for attendance; when finished they divide and stand in attendance below the red steps—the formation known as the Moth-Eyebrow Formation.

sentences.zh: 然後宰相率正班入起居，雅合於禮。

translations.literal: Only then do the chief ministers lead the full court in for attendance—this is fully in accord with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Only then should the chief ministers lead the full court in for attendance—fully in accord with proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞古之王者，躬勤庶務，其臨朝之疏數，視政事之繁簡。

translations.literal: I have also heard that the kings of antiquity personally attended to every task; the frequency of their audiences depended on whether affairs of state were numerous or few.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that the kings of antiquity personally attended to the myriad tasks of government; how often they held court depended on whether public business was heavy or light.

sentences.zh: 唐初五日一朝，景雲初，始修貞觀故事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang, audiences were held once every five days; at the beginning of the Jingyun era the Zhenguan precedent was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tang dynasty the emperor held court every five days; at the opening of the Jingyun era the Zhenguan precedent was restored.

sentences.zh: 自天寶兵興之後，四方多故，肅宗而下，咸隻日臨朝，雙日不坐。

translations.literal: After the outbreak of war in the Tianbao era troubles multiplied on every side; from Emperor Suzong downward, all held court on alternate days and did not sit for audiences on the intervening days.
translations.idiomatic: After warfare erupted in the Tianbao era and troubles multiplied everywhere, emperors from Suzong onward held court on alternate days, resting on the days between.

sentences.zh: 其隻日或遇陰霪、盛暑、大寒、泥濘，亦放百官起居。

translations.literal: On days when court was held, if there was rain, extreme heat, severe cold, or muddy roads, attendance for all officials was also waived.
translations.idiomatic: On court days, rain, extreme heat, severe cold, or muddy roads could also excuse officials from attendance.

sentences.zh: 雙日宰相當奏事，即特開延英召對。

translations.literal: On non-court days, when chief ministers were due to report affairs, the Yingying Hall would be specially opened for audience and consultation.
translations.idiomatic: On off days, when chief ministers were scheduled to report affairs, the Yingying Hall would be specially opened for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 或夷蠻入貢，勳臣歸朝，亦特開紫宸殿引見。

translations.literal: When tribal envoys presented tribute or meritorious ministers returned to court, the Zichen Hall would also be specially opened for audience.
translations.idiomatic: When tribal envoys arrived with tribute or meritorious ministers returned to court, the Zichen Hall would be opened for special audience.

sentences.zh: 陛下自臨大寶，十有五年，未嘗一日不雞鳴而起，聽天下之政，雖剛健不息，固天德之常然，而遊焉息焉，亦聖人之謨訓。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has personally borne the great burden for fifteen years, not once failing to rise at cockcrow and hear the governance of all under Heaven; though vigor without cease is indeed the constant virtue of Heaven, to wander and to rest is also the sage's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has personally borne the imperial burden for fifteen years, rising at cockcrow every day without exception to hear the governance of the realm; though tireless vigor is indeed Heaven's constant virtue, repose and ease are likewise the sage's teaching.

sentences.zh: 儻君父焦勞於上，臣子緘默於下，不能引大體以爭，則忠良之心，有所不至矣。

translations.literal: If the lord and father toils in distress above while ministers and sons remain silent below and cannot appeal to broader principle in debate, then the hearts of the loyal and good cannot reach their full measure.
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign exhausts himself above while his ministers hold their tongues below, unable to appeal to larger principle, then the loyalty of the good cannot find its fullest expression.

sentences.zh: 臣欲望陛下依前代舊規，隻日視朝，雙日不坐。

translations.literal: Your servant desires that Your Majesty follow the old regulations of former dynasties: hold court on alternate days and rest on the days between.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty restore the regulations of earlier dynasties—holding court on alternate days and resting between.

sentences.zh: 其隻日遇大寒、盛暑、陰霪、泥濘，亦放百官起居，其雙日於崇德、崇政兩殿召對宰臣。

translations.literal: On court days, if there is severe cold, extreme heat, rain, or muddy roads, attendance for all officials is also waived; on off days chief ministers are summoned for deliberation in the Chongde and Chongzheng Halls.
translations.idiomatic: On court days, severe cold, extreme heat, rain, or muddy roads should likewise excuse officials from attendance; on off days chief ministers should be summoned to the Chongde and Chongzheng Halls for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 常參官以下及非時蠻夷入貢、勳臣歸朝，亦特開上閤引見，並請準前代故事處分。」

translations.literal: For regular officials below that rank, and for unscheduled tribal tribute or the return of meritorious ministers, the Upper Gate should also be specially opened for audience—all to be handled according to the precedents of earlier dynasties."
translations.idiomatic: Regular officials below that rank, unscheduled tribal tribute missions, and the return of meritorious ministers should likewise receive special audience at the Upper Gate—all governed by the precedents of earlier dynasties."

sentences.zh: 奏入不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted without response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 時上令以《儒行篇》刻於版，印賜近臣及新第舉人。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor ordered the 'Conduct of the Scholar' chapter carved on a block and printed copies distributed to close ministers and newly passed examination candidates.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ordered the 'Conduct of the Scholar' carved on blocks and copies printed for distribution to close ministers and newly successful examination candidates.

sentences.zh: 洎得之，上表稱謝，上覽而嘉之。

translations.literal: When Ji received his copy he submitted a memorial of thanks; the emperor read it and commended it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji received a copy and submitted a memorial of thanks; the emperor read it with approval.

sentences.zh: 翌日，謂宰相曰：「群臣上章獻文，朕無不再三省覽。

translations.literal: The next day he told the chief ministers: 'When officials submit memorials and essays, there is none I do not read three times.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told the chief ministers: 'Every memorial and essay submitted to me I read over thrice.

sentences.zh: 如張洎一表，援引古今，甚不可得。

translations.literal: A memorial such as Zhang Ji's, drawing on ancient and modern precedents, is truly hard to come by.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial like Zhang Ji's, drawing on ancient and modern precedent, is truly a rarity.

sentences.zh: 可召至中書，宣諭朕意。」

translations.literal: Summon him to the Secretariat and convey my sentiments.'
translations.idiomatic: Summon him to the Secretariat and convey my sentiments.'

sentences.zh: 數月，擢拜中書舍人，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: Several months later he was promoted to Drafting Secretary and appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was promoted to Drafting Secretary and appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 上顧謂近臣曰：「學士之職，清要貴重，非他官可比，朕常恨不得為之。」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to his close attendants and said: 'The post of academician is pure, essential, and honored—it cannot be compared with other offices; I often regret that I cannot be one myself.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remarked to his close attendants: 'The post of Hanlin Academician is refined, weighty, and distinguished beyond any other office—I often wish I could hold it myself.'

sentences.zh: 故事，赴上日設燕，教坊以雜戲進，久罷其事。

translations.literal: By precedent a banquet was held on the day of entering office, and the Music Bureau would present miscellaneous performances; this practice had long been discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: By old precedent a banquet was held on the day of taking office, with the Music Bureau performing varied entertainments—a practice long discontinued.

sentences.zh: 至是，令盡設之，仍詔樞密直學士呂端、劉昌言及知制誥柴成務等預會，時以為榮。

translations.literal: On this occasion all was fully restored, and Hanlin Academicians in the Privy Council Lü Duan and Liu Changyan together with Edict-Drafter Chai Chengwu and others were ordered to attend—at the time this was considered a great honor.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion the full ceremony was restored, and Privy Council Hanlin Academicians Lü Duan and Liu Changyan, Edict-Drafter Chai Chengwu, and others were invited—an honor widely envied at the time.

sentences.zh: 俄判吏部銓。

translations.literal: Before long he also directed the Ministry of Personnel's selection office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also put in charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection office.

sentences.zh: 嘗引對選人，上顧之謂近臣曰：「張洎富有文藝，至今尚苦學，江東士人之冠也。」

translations.literal: Once when conducting audience with examination candidates, the emperor turned and said to close attendants: 'Zhang Ji is richly endowed with literary talent and to this day still studies assiduously—the foremost scholar of the Jiangdong region.'
translations.idiomatic: Once during audience with examination candidates the emperor remarked to his attendants: 'Zhang Ji possesses rich literary gifts and still labors at his studies—he is the foremost scholar of Jiangdong.'

sentences.zh: 洎與錢若水同在禁林，甚被寵顧。

translations.literal: Ji together with Qian Ruoshui served in the Forbidden Grove and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Ji served in the Forbidden Grove alongside Qian Ruoshui and enjoyed great imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 時劉昌言驟擢樞要，人望甚輕，董儼方掌財賦，欲以計傾之。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Changyan had risen rapidly to a pivotal post and was lightly regarded by public opinion; Dong Yan had recently taken charge of finance and wished through stratagem to undermine him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyan had risen rapidly to a pivotal post and was lightly regarded at court; Dong Yan, who had recently assumed control of finance, sought to undermine him by intrigue.

sentences.zh: 會楊徽之、錢熙嘗言洎及若水旦夕當大用。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Huizhi and Qian Xi had once said that Ji and Ruoshui would soon be greatly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huizhi and Qian Xi had once remarked that Ji and Ruoshui would soon rise to high office.

sentences.zh: 熙以語昌言，昌言曰：「洎必參政柄。

translations.literal: Xi told this to Changyan, and Changyan said: 'Ji will surely wield political power.
translations.idiomatic: Xi relayed this to Changyan, who replied: 'Ji is sure to wield political power.

sentences.zh: 若水後進年少，豈遽及此。」

translations.literal: Ruoshui is a junior still young in years—how could he suddenly reach this rank?'
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui is junior and young—how could he rise so quickly?'

sentences.zh: 時翰林小吏諮事在側，昌言慮洎聞之，即對小吏盡述熙言，令告洎。

translations.literal: At that time a minor Hanlin clerk seeking instructions was standing nearby; Changyan, fearing Ji might hear of it, immediately told the clerk everything Xi had said and ordered him to inform Ji.
translations.idiomatic: A minor Hanlin clerk seeking instructions happened to be nearby; fearing Ji might hear of the remark, Changyan immediately repeated Xi's entire statement to the clerk and told him to report it to Ji.

sentences.zh: 洎方修飭邊幅以固恩寵，疑徽之遣熙以構飛語中己，遂白於上。

translations.literal: Ji was at that time cultivating his personal conduct to secure imperial favor; suspecting that Huizhi had sent Xi to fabricate slander to harm him, he reported the matter to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was then carefully cultivating his public persona to secure imperial favor; suspecting Huizhi had sent Xi to invent slander against him, he reported the affair to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上怒，召昌言質之，以徽之為鎮安軍行軍司馬，熙罷職，通判朗州。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, summoned Changyan to confront him, appointed Huizhi Staff Adjutant of the Zhen'an Army, dismissed Xi from office, and posted him as Vice Prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. Changyan was summoned for questioning; Huizhi was demoted to Staff Adjutant of the Zhen'an Army; Xi was dismissed and posted as Vice Prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 會皇子益王元傑改封吳王，行揚州、潤州大都督府長史，領淮南、鎮江兩軍節制。

translations.literal: When the prince Yijian, styled Prince of Yi, was redesignated Prince of Wu, he served as Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou and Runzhou Superior Command and controlled the Huainan and Zhenjiang armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yijian of Yi was redesignated Prince of Wu, he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou and Runzhou Superior Command and given control of the Huainan and Zhenjiang armies.

sentences.zh: 洎當草制，因上疏議曰：「謹按前史，皇子封王，以郡為國，置傅相及內史、中尉等，佐王為治。

translations.literal: Ji was to draft the edict and therefore submitted a memorial arguing: 'Respectfully citing earlier histories, when a prince was enfeoffed as king, a commandery served as his state and tutors, chancellors, inner secretaries, commandants, and the like were appointed to assist the king in governance.
translations.idiomatic: As Ji was tasked with drafting the edict, he submitted a memorial arguing: 'Historical precedent shows that when a prince is enfeoffed as king, a commandery becomes his state; tutors, chancellors, inner secretaries, and commandants are appointed to assist in governance.

sentences.zh: 自漢、魏以降，所封之王始不之國，朝廷命卿大夫臨郡，即稱內史行郡事。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei downward the kings enfeoffed no longer went to their states; the court appointed grand masters to administer the commanderies, styled as inner secretaries conducting commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei onward enfeoffed kings no longer went to their states; the court instead appointed grand masters to administer the commanderies, styled as inner secretaries conducting commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 東晉永和、泰元之際，有琅邪王、會稽王、臨川王，故謝靈運、王羲之等為會稽、臨川內史，即其事也。

translations.literal: At the time of the Yonghe and Taiyuan eras in Eastern Jin there were the Princes of Langye, Kuaiji, and Linchuan—hence Xie Lingyun and Wang Xizhi served as inner secretaries of Kuaiji and Linchuan; this is the precedent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghe and Taiyuan eras of Eastern Jin there were the Princes of Langye, Kuaiji, and Linchuan—hence Xie Lingyun and Wang Xizhi served as inner secretaries of Kuaiji and Linchuan, exactly this case.

sentences.zh: 唐有天下，以揚、益、潞、幽、荊五郡為大都督，署長史、司馬為上佐，即前代內史之類也。

translations.literal: When Tang held the realm, Yang, Yi, Lu, You, and Jing were made superior commands, with chief administrators and vice administrators as senior aides—equivalent to the inner secretaries of earlier dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, Yang, Yi, Lu, You, and Jing were made superior commands, with chief administrators and vice administrators as senior aides—the equivalent of earlier inner secretaries.

sentences.zh: 其大都督之號，非親王不授；

translations.literal: The title of superior commander was granted to none but imperial princes;
translations.idiomatic: The title of superior commander was granted only to imperial princes;

sentences.zh: 其揚、益等郡，或有親王遙領，朝廷命大臣臨郡者，即皆長史、副大使知節度事也。

translations.literal: For Yang, Yi, and other commanderies, when an imperial prince held nominal command while the court appointed a senior minister to administer the commandery, these were all styled vice ambassadors directing military commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Where an imperial prince held nominal command over Yang, Yi, and other regions while a senior minister administered the commandery on the court's behalf, they were styled vice ambassadors directing military commission affairs.

sentences.zh: 臣請質之前代，段文昌出鎮揚州，云『淮南節度副大使知節度事、兼揚州大都督府長史』、李載義鎮幽州，云『盧龍軍節度副大使知節度事、兼幽州大都督府長史』，即其例也。

translations.literal: Your servant requests verification against earlier generations: when Duan Wenchang was stationed at Yangzhou the title read 'Vice Ambassador of the Huainan Military Commission directing military commission affairs and concurrently Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Superior Command'; when Li Zaiyi was stationed at Youzhou it read 'Vice Ambassador of the Lulong Army Military Commission directing military commission affairs and concurrently Chief Administrator of the Youzhou Superior Command'—these are the precedents.
translations.idiomatic: I cite earlier precedent: when Duan Wenchang took command at Yangzhou his title read 'Vice Ambassador of the Huainan Military Commission directing military commission affairs and concurrently Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Superior Command'; when Li Zaiyi held Youzhou, 'Vice Ambassador of the Lulong Army Military Commission directing military commission affairs and concurrently Chief Administrator of the Youzhou Superior Command.' These are the models.

sentences.zh: 今益王以揚、潤二郡建社為吳國王，居大都督之任，又己正領節度事，豈宜卻加長史之號，乃是國王自為上佐矣。

translations.literal: Now Prince Yi, with Yang and Run as his two commanderies, establishing his fief as Prince of Wu, occupying the post of superior commander while already directly controlling military commission affairs—how can he additionally be given the title of chief administrator? This would make the king his own senior aide.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi, with Yang and Run as his two commanderies and enfeoffed as Prince of Wu, already holds the post of superior commander and directly commands military commission affairs—how can he also bear the title of chief administrator? That would make the prince his own senior aide.

sentences.zh: 若或朝廷且以長史拜受，其加銜內又無副大使、知節度使之目，倘或他日別命守將，俾臨本郡，即不知以何名目而授除也。

translations.literal: If for the moment the court grants the title of chief administrator, yet within the additional honorific there is no designation of vice ambassador or director of military commission affairs, then if someday the court separately appoints a garrison commander to administer this commandery, it would be unclear under what title to grant the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: If the court temporarily grants the title of chief administrator, yet the honorific includes no designation as vice ambassador or director of military commission affairs, then if the court later appoints a separate garrison commander to administer the commandery, under what title would the appointment be made?

sentences.zh: 臣草制之夕，便欲上陳，慮奏報往反，有妨明日宣降。

translations.literal: On the evening Your servant was drafting the edict I wished to report this at once, but feared that the exchange of memorials and responses would interfere with promulgation the next day.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening I was drafting the edict I wished to report at once, but feared that memorials going back and forth might delay promulgation the next day.

sentences.zh: 茲事有關國體，況吳王未領恩命，尚可改正，乞付中書門下，商議施行。」

translations.literal: This matter concerns the dignity of the state; moreover Prince Wu has not yet received his gracious commission and the matter can still be corrected—I beg that it be sent to the Secretariat and Chancellery for deliberation and implementation.'
translations.idiomatic: This touches the dignity of the state; Prince Wu has not yet received his commission and the matter can still be corrected. I pray it be referred to the Secretariat and Chancellery for deliberation.'

sentences.zh: 宰相以制命已行，難於追改。

translations.literal: The chief ministers held that the edict had already been promulgated and was difficult to reverse.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers held that since the edict had already been issued, reversal would be difficult.

sentences.zh: 洎又上表論列，呂蒙正言：「越王領福州長史，今吳王獨為大都督，居越王之上，非便。」

translations.literal: Ji submitted another memorial arguing the point; Lü Mengzheng said: 'The Prince of Yue holds the post of Chief Administrator of Fuzhou; now the Prince of Wu alone is made superior commander, placing him above the Prince of Yue—inconvenient.'
translations.idiomatic: Ji submitted another memorial on the point. Lü Mengzheng argued: 'The Prince of Yue holds the post of Chief Administrator of Fuzhou; making the Prince of Wu alone a superior commander would place him above the Prince of Yue—an awkward arrangement.'

sentences.zh: 上令俟異日除授，並改正之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that when new appointments were granted on another day, all would be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that corrections be made at the next round of appointments.

sentences.zh: 至明年，上郊祀覃慶，遂改焉。

translations.literal: The following year, when the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice and proclaimed a general amnesty, the matter was revised.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice and proclaimed a general amnesty, the titles were revised.

sentences.zh: 俄奉詔與李至、范杲、張佖同修國史，又判史館。

translations.literal: Before long he received an edict to compile the National History together with Li Zhi, Fan Gao, and Zhang Bi, and again directed the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he received an edict to compile the National History with Li Zhi, Fan Gao, and Zhang Bi, and again directed the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 洎博涉經史，多知典故。

translations.literal: Ji ranged broadly through the classics and histories and knew many precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Ji ranged broadly through the classics and histories and possessed deep knowledge of precedent.

sentences.zh: 每上有著述，或賜近臣詩什，洎必上表，援引經傳，以將順其意。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor composed a work or bestowed verse on close ministers, Ji invariably submitted a memorial citing the classics and commentaries to accord with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor composed a work or bestowed verse on close ministers, Ji would submit a memorial citing the classics to echo the imperial sentiment.

sentences.zh: 上因賜詩褒美，有「翰長老儒臣」之句。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore bestowed a poem in praise, containing the line 'venerable scholar of the Hanlin chief.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed a poem in praise containing the line 'venerable scholar-chancellor of the Hanlin.'

sentences.zh: 與蘇易簡同在翰林，尤不協，及易簡參知政事，洎多攻其失。

translations.literal: He was especially at odds with Su Yijian, who also served in the Hanlin; when Yijian became Participation Grand Councillor, Ji frequently attacked his faults.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially at odds with Su Yijian, his fellow Hanlin Academician; when Yijian became Participation Grand Councillor, Ji frequently attacked his failings.

sentences.zh: 既而易簡罷，即以洎為給事中、參知政事，與寇準同列。

translations.literal: Before long Yijian was dismissed, and Ji was appointed Supervising Censor and Participation Grand Councillor, serving in the same rank as Kou Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yijian was dismissed, and Ji was appointed Supervising Censor and Participation Grand Councillor, serving alongside Kou Zhun.

sentences.zh: 先是，準知吏部選事，洎掌考功，為吏部官屬。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhun directed selection affairs in the Ministry of Personnel while Ji managed merit review—they were both subordinates within the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Kou Zhun had directed selection affairs in the Ministry of Personnel while Ji managed merit review—both serving within that ministry.

sentences.zh: 準年少，新進氣銳，思欲老儒附己以自大。

translations.literal: Zhun was young, newly risen and sharp in spirit, and wished to have senior scholars attach themselves to him to magnify himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun was young, newly risen, and ambitious; he wished senior scholars to attach themselves to him so he might magnify his standing.

sentences.zh: 洎夙夜坐曹視事，每冠帶候準出入於省門，揖而退，不交一談。

translations.literal: Ji attended to affairs at his desk day and night; each time, fully robed and capped, he waited at the ministry gate for Zhun's comings and goings, bowed, and withdrew—never exchanging a word.
translations.idiomatic: Ji attended to his duties day and night; each day, fully robed, he waited at the ministry gate for Zhun's comings and goings, bowed, and withdrew without ever exchanging a word.

sentences.zh: 準益重焉，因延與語。

translations.literal: Zhun regarded him all the more highly and invited him to converse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun came to respect him all the more and invited him to talk.

sentences.zh: 洎捷給善持論，多為準規畫，準心伏，乃兄事之，極口談洎於上。

translations.literal: Ji was quick-witted and skilled in debate, and often made plans for Zhun; Zhun was won over in his heart, treated him as an elder brother, and spoke of Ji to the emperor at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and skilled in argument, Ji often drafted plans for Zhun; deeply impressed, Zhun treated him as an elder brother and spoke of him to the emperor at every opportunity.

sentences.zh: 上欲進用，又知其在江左日多讒毀良善，李煜殺潘佑，洎嘗預謀，心疑之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to promote him, yet knew that in his Jiangzuo days he had often slandered the good; when Li Yu killed Pan You, Ji had once participated in the plot—the emperor harbored doubts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to promote him but knew that during his Jiangzuo days he had often slandered good men; when Li Yu killed Pan You, Ji had reportedly been involved—so the emperor hesitated.

sentences.zh: 翰林待詔尹熙古、吳郢皆江東人，洎嘗善待之。

translations.literal: Hanlin Attendant-Candidates Yin Xigu and Wu Ying were both from Jiangdong, and Ji had often treated them well.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Attendant-Candidates Yin Xigu and Wu Ying, both from Jiangdong, had long enjoyed Ji's favor.

sentences.zh: 上一夕召熙古輩侍書禁中，因問以佑得罪故。

translations.literal: One evening the emperor summoned Xigu and the others to attend him in writing within the Forbidden Palace and asked them the reason for You's offense.
translations.idiomatic: One evening the emperor summoned Xigu and the others to serve him in writing within the palace and asked why Pan You had fallen from grace.

sentences.zh: 熙古言煜忿佑諫說太直耳，非洎謀也。

translations.literal: Xigu said Li Yu resented You because his remonstrances were too blunt—it was not Ji's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Xigu said Li Yu resented Pan You because his counsel was too blunt—it was not Ji's doing.

sentences.zh: 自是洗然，遂加擢用，蓋準推挽之也。

translations.literal: From then on the emperor's doubts cleared, and Ji was promoted—largely through Zhun's advocacy.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the emperor's doubts cleared, and Ji was promoted—largely through Kou Zhun's advocacy.

sentences.zh: 既同秉政，奉準愈謹，政事一決於準，無所參預。

translations.literal: Once they jointly held power, Ji was deferential to Zhun in the extreme; all affairs of government were decided by Zhun, and Ji took no part.
translations.idiomatic: Once they shared power, Ji deferred to Zhun utterly; all government affairs were decided by Zhun alone, with Ji taking no part.

sentences.zh: 專修時政記，甘言善柔而已。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to compiling the Record of Current Governance, offering only honeyed words and soft flattery.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to compiling the Record of Current Governance, offering nothing but flattery and soft words.

sentences.zh: 後因奏事異同，準復忌之。

translations.literal: Later, because they differed when reporting affairs, Zhun again came to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when they differed in reporting on affairs of state, Kou Zhun came to resent him again.

sentences.zh: 至道二年五月，四方館使曹璨自河西馳騎入奏邊事，言繼遷率萬餘眾寇靈州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Zhidao, Envoy Cao Shen of the Four Directions Office rode in from the Hexi corridor to report on frontier affairs, stating that Jiqian was leading more than ten thousand men to raid Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of 996, Cao Shen, envoy of the Four Directions Office, rode in from the Hexi corridor to report frontier affairs: Jiqian was leading more than ten thousand men against Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上詔宰相呂端、知樞密院事趙鎔等各以所見畫策，即日具奏來上。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Chief Minister Lü Duan, Privy Council Commissioner Zhao Yong, and the others each to formulate strategy according to their views and submit memorials that same day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chief Minister Lü Duan, Privy Council Commissioner Zhao Yong, and others each to submit strategy according to their judgment that very day.

sentences.zh: 呂端相率詣長春殿見上，言曰：「臣等若各述所見，則非詢謀僉同之議，望許其為一狀，陳其利害。」

translations.literal: Lü Duan together led them to the Changchun Hall to see the emperor and said: 'If each of us states his own view separately, it will not be deliberation with unanimous agreement; we request permission to submit one memorial together setting forth advantages and disadvantages.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Duan led them to the Changchun Hall and said: 'If each of us states his own view, it cannot constitute joint deliberation; we ask permission to submit a single memorial setting forth costs and benefits.'

sentences.zh: 洎越次奏曰：「端等備位輔弼，上有所詢問，反緘默不言，深失訏謨之體。」

translations.literal: Ji stepped forward out of order and submitted: 'Duan and the others hold posts as chief ministers; when the emperor makes inquiries, they instead remain silent—this deeply fails the standard of planning and deliberation.'
translations.idiomatic: Ji interrupted and submitted: 'Duan and his colleagues hold the highest ministerial posts; when the sovereign inquires, they remain silent—a grave failure of counsel and deliberation.'

sentences.zh: 端曰：「洎欲有言，不過揣摩陛下意耳，必無鯁切之理。」

translations.literal: Duan said: 'If Ji wishes to speak, it will be nothing but guessing at Your Majesty's intent—certainly nothing bluntly candid.'
translations.idiomatic: Duan replied: 'Whatever Ji has to say will be nothing but a guess at Your Majesty's mind—hardly frank counsel.'

sentences.zh: 上默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 翌日，洎上疏引賈捐之棄珠崖事，願棄靈武以省關西饋運。

translations.literal: The next day Ji submitted a memorial citing Jia Juan's abandonment of Zhuya, proposing to abandon Lingwu to economize on supply transport from Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ji submitted a memorial citing Jia Juan's abandonment of Zhuya, proposing to abandon Lingwu and thereby reduce the burden of supply transport from Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 上嘗有此意，既而悔之，洎果迎合，覽奏不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor had once held this intention, then regretted it; Ji had exactly pandered to it, and reading the memorial he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had once entertained this idea, then thought better of it; Ji had precisely seconded it, and on reading the memorial he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 既以疏付洎，謂之曰：「卿所陳，朕不曉一句。」

translations.literal: He returned the memorial to Ji and said: 'What you set forth—I do not understand a single sentence of it.'
translations.idiomatic: He returned the memorial to Ji and said, 'What you wrote—I cannot make sense of a single sentence.'

sentences.zh: 洎惶恐而退。

translations.literal: Ji withdrew in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Ji withdrew in terror.

sentences.zh: 上召同知樞密院事向敏中等謂曰：「張洎上言，果為呂端所料，朕已還其疏矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Privy Council Vice Commissioner Xiang Minzhong and others and said: 'Zhang Ji's memorial was exactly as Lü Duan predicted; I have already returned it to him.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Privy Council Vice Commissioner Xiang Minzhong and others and said, 'Zhang Ji's memorial was exactly as Lü Duan foretold—I have already returned it to him.'

sentences.zh: 洎既議事不稱旨，恐懼，欲自固權位。

translations.literal: Having failed to satisfy the emperor in deliberation, Ji was fearful and sought to secure his own position of power.
translations.idiomatic: Having displeased the emperor in deliberation, Ji grew fearful and sought to shore up his own standing.

sentences.zh: 上已嫉準專恣，恩寵衰替。

translations.literal: The emperor already resented Zhun's arrogance and self-will; imperial favor toward him was waning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already resented Kou Zhun's arrogance, and imperial favor toward him was fading.

sentences.zh: 洎慮一旦同罷免，因奏事，大言寇準退後多誹謗。

translations.literal: Fearing they might both be dismissed at once, Ji took an opportunity while reporting affairs to declare loudly that Kou Zhun often slandered others after leaving court.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing they might both be dismissed together, Ji seized an occasion while reporting affairs to declare that Kou Zhun often slandered others after leaving court.

sentences.zh: 準但色變，不敢自辯。

translations.literal: Zhun only changed color; he did not dare defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun only changed color and did not dare defend himself.

sentences.zh: 上由是大怒，準旬日罷。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered thereby; within ten days Zhun was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious; within ten days Kou Zhun was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，洎病在告，滿百日，力疾請對，方拜，踣於上前，左右掖起之。

translations.literal: Before long Ji fell ill and took leave; when the hundred days were complete he forced himself, ill as he was, to request audience; as he bowed he collapsed before the emperor, and attendants helped him up.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ji fell ill and took leave; when the hundred days were up he forced himself, sick as he was, to request audience—then collapsed before the emperor as he bowed, and attendants had to help him up.

sentences.zh: 明日，上章求解職，優詔不允。

translations.literal: The next day he submitted a memorial requesting release from office; a gracious edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he submitted a memorial asking to be relieved of office; a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 後月餘，改刑部侍郎，罷知政事。

translations.literal: A month or so later he was reassigned as Vice Minister of Justice and removed from participation in government.
translations.idiomatic: A month or so later he was reassigned Vice Minister of Justice and removed from participation in government.

sentences.zh: 奉詔嗚咽，疾遂亟，十餘日卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: Upon receiving the edict he wept; his illness grew acute, and within a dozen days he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: On receiving the edict he wept aloud; his illness turned grave, and within a dozen days he died, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈刑部尚書，以其二子皆為京官。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was honored as Minister of Justice, and both his sons were granted metropolitan posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored Minister of Justice, and both his sons were granted metropolitan posts.

sentences.zh: 洎風儀灑落，文采清麗，博覽道釋書，兼通禪寂虛無之理。

translations.literal: Ji carried himself with easy grace; his literary style was clear and elegant. He ranged widely through Daoist and Buddhist texts and was versed in Chan quietism and the philosophy of emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Ji carried himself with easy grace and wrote in a clear, elegant style. He read widely in Daoist and Buddhist literature and was versed in Chan quietism and the philosophy of emptiness.

sentences.zh: 終日清談，亹亹可聽。

translations.literal: All day long he held refined conversation—eloquent and pleasing to hear.
translations.idiomatic: All day long he held refined conversation—flowing and pleasant to hear.

sentences.zh: 尤險詖，好攻人之短。

translations.literal: He was especially treacherous and malicious, fond of attacking others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially treacherous and malicious, fond of attacking others' faults.

sentences.zh: 李煜既歸朝，貧甚，洎猶丐索之。

translations.literal: After Li Yu submitted to the dynasty he was very poor, yet Ji still begged and demanded things of him.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Yu submitted to the dynasty he was destitute, yet Ji still begged and demanded things of him.

sentences.zh: 煜以白金摐面器與洎，洎尚未滿意。

translations.literal: Yu gave Ji a white-gold face-washing vessel; still Ji was not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu gave Ji a white-gold face-washing vessel, but Ji was still not satisfied.

sentences.zh: 時潘慎脩掌煜記室，洎疑慎脩教煜，素與慎脩善，自是亦稍疏之。

translations.literal: At the time Pan Shenxiu managed Yu's secretariat; Ji suspected Shenxiu had coached Yu. Though once on good terms with Shenxiu, from then on he kept some distance.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Pan Shenxiu managed Li Yu's secretariat; Ji suspected Shenxiu had coached him. Though once on good terms with Shenxiu, from then on he kept his distance.

sentences.zh: 煜子仲㝢雅好蒱博飲宴，洎因切諫之，仲㝢謝過。

translations.literal: Yu's son Zhongyu was fond of gambling, wine, and banquets; Ji remonstrated sharply, and Zhongyu apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu's son Zhongyu was fond of gambling, wine, and banquets; Ji remonstrated sharply, and Zhongyu apologized.

sentences.zh: 後數月，人有言仲㝢蒱博如故，洎遂與之絕。

translations.literal: Months later someone said Zhongyu gambled as before; Ji then severed relations with him.
translations.idiomatic: Months later someone reported that Zhongyu gambled as before; Ji then broke off relations with him.

sentences.zh: 及仲㝢死郢州，葬京師，洎亦不赴吊。

translations.literal: When Zhongyu died at Yingzhou and was buried in the capital, Ji did not attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongyu died at Yingzhou and was buried in the capital, Ji did not attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 與張佖議事不協，遂為讐隙，始以從父禮事佖，既而不拜。

translations.literal: He disagreed with Zhang Bi on affairs of state and they became enemies; at first he treated Bi with the courtesy due an uncle, but later ceased to bow.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with Zhang Bi over policy and they became enemies; at first he treated Bi with the courtesy due an uncle, but later ceased to bow to him.

sentences.zh: 尤善事內官，在翰林日，引唐故事，奏內供奉官藍敏政為學士使，內侍裴愈副之。

translations.literal: He was especially adept at cultivating eunuchs; while in the Hanlin he cited Tang precedent and memorialized that Inner Attendant Lan Minzheng be made Hanlin envoy, with Inner Attendant Pei Yu as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at cultivating eunuchs; while in the Hanlin he cited Tang precedent and memorialized that Inner Attendant Lan Minzheng be made Hanlin envoy, with Inner Attendant Pei Yu as deputy.

sentences.zh: 上覽奏，謂曰：「此唐室弊政，朕安可踵此覆轍，卿言過也。」

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and said: 'This was a corrupt policy of Tang—how can I follow that ruinous path? Your proposal goes too far.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and said, 'This was a corrupt policy of Tang—how can I follow that ruinous path? Your proposal goes too far.'

sentences.zh: 洎慚而退。

translations.literal: Ji withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ji withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 性鄙吝，雖親戚無所霑，及江表故舊，亦罕登其門。

translations.literal: By nature he was petty and stingy; kin received nothing from him, and old friends from the lower Yang region rarely crossed his threshold.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was petty and stingy; even kin received nothing from him, and old friends from the Jiangnan region rarely crossed his threshold.

sentences.zh: 素與徐鉉厚善，後因議事相忤，遂絕交。

translations.literal: He had long been close to Xu Xuan, but later they clashed over policy and broke off relations.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been close to Xu Xuan, but later they clashed over policy and broke off relations.

sentences.zh: 然手寫鉉文章，訪求其筆劄，藏篋笥，甚於珍玩。

translations.literal: Yet he copied Xuan's essays by hand, sought out his letters, and stored them in boxes as treasured curios.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he copied Xuan's essays by hand, sought out his letters, and stored them in boxes as treasured curios.

sentences.zh: 洎有文集五十卷行於世。

translations.literal: Ji's collected works, fifty juan, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's collected works, fifty juan, circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子安期，至國子博士；

translations.literal: His son Anqi rose to Doctor of the National University;
translations.idiomatic: His son Anqi rose to Doctor of the National University;

sentences.zh: 方回，後為虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: Fanghui later served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Fanghui later served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 方回子懷玉，王欽若婿，賜進士及第，大理寺丞，秘書校理。

translations.literal: Fanghui's son Huaiyu, son-in-law of Wang Qinruo, was granted jinshi rank, served as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, and as collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Fanghui's son Huaiyu, son-in-law of Wang Qinruo, was granted jinshi rank and served as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李惟清

translations.literal: Li Weiqing
translations.idiomatic: Li Weiqing

sentences.zh: 李惟清，字直臣，下邑人。

translations.literal: Li Weiqing, styled Zhichen, was a native of Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Weiqing, styled Zhichen, was a native of Xiayi.

sentences.zh: 父仲行，為章丘簿，因徙家焉。

translations.literal: His father Zhongxing served as registrar of Zhangqiu; the family relocated there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongxing served as registrar of Zhangqiu, and the family moved there.

sentences.zh: 惟清，開寶中，以三史解褐涪陵尉。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao era Weiqing entered service through the Three Histories examination as assistant magistrate of Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era Weiqing entered service through the Three Histories examination as assistant magistrate of Fuling.

sentences.zh: 蜀民尚淫祀，病不療治，聽於巫覡，惟清擒大巫笞之，民以為及禍。

translations.literal: The people of Shu favored excessive sacrificial cults; when ill they did not seek medical treatment but obeyed shamans. Weiqing seized the chief shaman and flogged him; the people believed calamity would follow.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu favored excessive sacrificial cults; when ill they did not seek medical treatment but obeyed shamans. Weiqing seized the chief shaman and flogged him, and the people believed calamity would follow.

sentences.zh: 他日又加箠焉，民知不神。

translations.literal: Another day he applied the cudgel again; the people knew the shamans had no power.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he applied the cudgel again, and the people knew the shamans had no power.

sentences.zh: 然後教以醫藥，稍變風俗。

translations.literal: Only then did he teach them medicine, and gradually the custom changed.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he teach them medicine, and gradually the custom changed.

sentences.zh: 時遣宦官督輸造船木，縱恣不法，惟清奏殺之，由是知名。

translations.literal: Eunuchs were then sent to supervise the delivery of shipbuilding timber; they acted lawlessly. Weiqing memorialized for their execution and became known thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs were then sent to supervise the delivery of shipbuilding timber and acted lawlessly. Weiqing memorialized for their execution and thereby became known.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，遷大理寺丞。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，遷為荊湖北路轉運判官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred as transport commissioner of the northern Hubei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred as transport commissioner of the northern Hubei circuit.

sentences.zh: 五年，改左讚善大夫，充轉運副使，升正使，就改監察御史，兼總南路。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Left Palmen of the Heir Apparent, vice transport commissioner, then full commissioner, and concurrently remonstrating censor overseeing the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Left Palmen of the Heir Apparent, vice transport commissioner, then full commissioner, and concurrently remonstrating censor overseeing the southern route.

sentences.zh: 嘗入奏事，太宗問曰：「荊湖累年豐稔，又無徭役，民間蘇否？」

translations.literal: Once when reporting to court, Taizong asked: 'The Jinghu region has enjoyed good harvests for years and bears no corvée—do the people prosper?'
translations.idiomatic: Once when reporting to court, Taizong asked, 'The Jinghu region has enjoyed good harvests for years and bears no corvée—do the people prosper?'

sentences.zh: 惟清曰：「臣見官賣鹽斤為錢六十四，民以三數斗稻價，方可買一斤。」

translations.literal: Weiqing said: 'I see official salt sold at sixty-four cash per jin; the people must pay the price of three or four dou of rice to buy one jin.'
translations.idiomatic: Weiqing said, 'I see official salt sold at sixty-four cash per jin—the people must pay the price of three or four dou of rice to buy a single jin.'

sentences.zh: 乃詔斤減十錢。

translations.literal: An edict then reduced the price by ten cash per jin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then reduced the price by ten cash per jin.

sentences.zh: 徙京西轉運使，入為度支判官，改主客員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred as transport commissioner of the western capital circuit, entered court as vice director of the Revenue Bureau, and was made vice director of the Ministry of Rites responsible for foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred transport commissioner of the western capital circuit, entered court as vice director of the Revenue Bureau, and was made vice director of the Ministry of Rites responsible for foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，大舉取幽州，惟清以為兵食未豐，不可輕動。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi a major campaign was launched against Youzhou; Weiqing held that provisions for the army were insufficient and the move should not be made lightly.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi a major campaign was launched against Youzhou; Weiqing held that army provisions were insufficient and the move should not be made lightly.

sentences.zh: 朝廷業已興師，奏入不報。

translations.literal: The court had already mobilized; his memorial received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already mobilized; his memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 判度支許仲宣建議通鹽法，以賣鹽歲課賦於鄉村，與戶稅均納。

translations.literal: Revenue Vice Director Xu Zhongxuan proposed a comprehensive salt law distributing the annual salt levy to villages to be paid alongside the household tax.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Vice Director Xu Zhongxuan proposed a comprehensive salt law distributing the annual salt levy to villages to be paid alongside the household tax.

sentences.zh: 惟清奉詔往荊湖諸路詳定，奏言以鹽配民非便，遂罷。

translations.literal: Weiqing was ordered to review the circuits of Jinghu and reported that assigning salt quotas to households was impracticable; the policy was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqing was ordered to review the Jinghu circuits and reported that assigning salt quotas to households was impracticable; the policy was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 使還，上又問民間苦樂不均事，惟清言：「前在荊湖，民市清酒務官釀轉鬻者，斗給耗二升，今三司給一升，民多他圖，而歲課甚減。」

translations.literal: Returning from his mission, the emperor again asked about unequal hardship among the people. Weiqing said: 'Previously in Jinghu, when the people bought liquor brewed and resold by the Clear Wine Bureau, two sheng per dou were allowed as wastage; now the Three Departments allow only one; the people find other channels and annual revenue has fallen sharply.'
translations.idiomatic: Returning from his mission, the emperor again asked about unequal hardship among the people. Weiqing said, 'Previously in Jinghu, when the people bought liquor brewed and resold by the Clear Wine Bureau, two sheng per dou were allowed as wastage; now the Three Departments allow only one—the people find other channels and annual revenue has fallen sharply.'

sentences.zh: 詔復其舊。

translations.literal: An edict restored the former allowance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored the former allowance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為京東轉運使。

translations.literal: Before long he was posted as transport commissioner of the eastern capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was posted as transport commissioner of the eastern capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 會募丁壯為義軍，惟清曰：若「是，天下不耕矣。」

translations.literal: When able-bodied men were being conscripted into volunteer armies, Weiqing said: 'If so, no one in the realm will farm.'
translations.idiomatic: When able-bodied men were being conscripted into volunteer armies, Weiqing said, 'If so, no one in the realm will farm.'

sentences.zh: 三上疏諫，繇是獨選河北，而餘路悉罷。

translations.literal: Three memorials of remonstrance followed; therefore only Hebei was selected, and all other circuits abandoned the policy.
translations.idiomatic: Three memorials of remonstrance followed; therefore only Hebei was selected, and all other circuits abandoned the policy.

sentences.zh: 擢屯田郎中、度支副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of Works and vice commissioner of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of Works and vice commissioner of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，遷右諫議大夫，歷戶部使，改度支使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was made Right Remonstrating Grand Master, then commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue, then commissioner of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong he was made Right Remonstrating Grand Master, then commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue, then commissioner of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 會遣使河朔治方田，大發兵。

translations.literal: Envoys were then sent to Hebei to administer equal-field land allocation, mobilizing troops on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were then sent to Hebei to administer equal-field land allocation, mobilizing troops on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 惟清以盛春妨農，懇求罷廢。

translations.literal: Weiqing held that peak spring farming season would be disrupted and urgently pleaded for abolition.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqing held that peak spring farming season would be disrupted and urgently pleaded for abolition.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「兵夫已發矣。

translations.literal: Taizong said: 'The labor troops have already been dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, 'The labor troops have already been dispatched.

sentences.zh: 止令完治邊城而已。」

translations.literal: Let them only complete repairs on the frontier walls.'
translations.idiomatic: Let them only complete repairs on the frontier walls.'

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，遷給事中，充鹽鐵使，遂以帳式奏御。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he was promoted to Supervising Censor and appointed salt and iron commissioner; he then submitted fiscal accounts to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua he was promoted Supervising Censor and appointed salt and iron commissioner, then submitted fiscal accounts to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「費用若此，民力久何以堪？

translations.literal: Taizong said: 'Expenditure at this level—how can the people's strength long endure it?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, 'Expenditure at this level—how can the people's strength long endure it?

sentences.zh: 如可減省，即便裁度。」

translations.literal: If reductions are possible, cut them at once.'
translations.idiomatic: If reductions are possible, cut them at once.'

sentences.zh: 惟清曰：「比開寶軍興之際，其數倍多，蓋以將帥未得其人，邊事未寧，屯兵至廣也。

translations.literal: Weiqing replied: 'Compared with the Kaibao era when war was launched, the figures are many times greater—because commanders were not the right men, the frontier was unsettled, and garrisons were vast.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqing replied, 'Compared with the Kaibao era when war was launched, the figures are many times greater—because commanders were not the right men, the frontier was unsettled, and garrisons were vast.

sentences.zh: 臣聞漢有衛青、霍去病，唐有郭子儀、李晟，西北望而畏之。

translations.literal: I have heard that Han had Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, Tang had Guo Ziyi and Li Sheng—the northwest looked upon them and trembled.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Han had Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, Tang had Guo Ziyi and Li Sheng—the northwest looked upon them and trembled.

sentences.zh: 如此則邊事息而支用減矣。

translations.literal: Then frontier troubles would cease and expenditure would fall.
translations.idiomatic: Then frontier troubles would cease and expenditure would fall.

sentences.zh: 望慎擢將帥，以有威名者俾安邊塞，庶節費用。」

translations.literal: I pray that generals be carefully selected—men of established renown to pacify the borderlands, so that costs may be trimmed.'
translations.idiomatic: I pray that generals be carefully selected—men of established renown to pacify the borderlands, so that costs may be trimmed.'

sentences.zh: 上言：「彼一時，此一時也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'That was one era; this is another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'That was one era; this is another.

sentences.zh: 今之西北變詐，與古不同。

translations.literal: The cunning and treachery of today's northwest differs from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The cunning and treachery of today's northwest differs from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 選用將帥，亦須深體今之幾宜。

translations.literal: In choosing commanders one must deeply grasp present circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: In choosing commanders one must deeply grasp present circumstances.

sentences.zh: 韓、彭雖古之名將，以彼時之見，制今之敵，亦恐不能成功。

translations.literal: Han Xin and Peng Yue, though famed generals of old—with the perspective of their age applied to today's enemy, success might still elude them.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin and Peng Yue, though famed generals of old—with the perspective of their age applied to today's enemy, success might still elude them.

sentences.zh: 今縱得人，未可便如古委之。

translations.literal: Even if the right men were found today, one could not simply delegate as in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the right men were found today, one could not simply delegate as in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 此乃機事，卿所未知也。」

translations.literal: These are matters of high strategy beyond your knowledge.'
translations.idiomatic: These are matters of high strategy beyond your knowledge.'

sentences.zh: 淮南榷貨務賣岳茶，斤為錢百五十。

translations.literal: The Huainan Monopoly Bureau sold Yue tea at one hundred fifty cash per jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan Monopoly Bureau sold Yue tea at one hundred fifty cash per jin.

sentences.zh: 主吏言陳惡者二十六萬六千餘斤，惟清擅減斤五十錢，不以聞。

translations.literal: The chief clerk reported 266,000-odd jin as spoiled; Weiqing on his own authority reduced the price by fifty cash per jin without reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk reported 266,000-odd jin as spoiled; Weiqing on his own authority reduced the price by fifty cash per jin without reporting it.

sentences.zh: 滁、泗、濠、楚州、漣水軍亦以岳茶陳惡，減價市之。

translations.literal: Chuzhou, Sizhou, Haozhou, Chuzhou, and Lianshui garrison likewise marked Yue tea as spoiled and bought it at reduced price.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou, Sizhou, Haozhou, Chuzhou, and Lianshui garrison likewise marked Yue tea as spoiled and bought it at reduced price.

sentences.zh: 計虧錢萬四千餘貫，為勾院吏盧守仁所發，左授衛尉少卿，黜判官李琯為本曹員外郎，賜守仁錢十五萬。

translations.literal: The loss totaled over fourteen thousand strings of cash; Auditing Bureau clerk Lu Shouren exposed it. Weiqing was demoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia; vice director Li Guan was relegated to a rank in his own bureau; Shouren was rewarded one hundred fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The loss totaled over fourteen thousand strings of cash; Auditing Bureau clerk Lu Shouren exposed it. Weiqing was demoted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia; vice director Li Guan was relegated to a rank in his own bureau; Shouren was rewarded one hundred fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 俄出知廣州。

translations.literal: Before long he was posted as prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was posted prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 至道初，就拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao he was directly appointed Right Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhidao he was directly appointed Right Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其廉平，詔獎之。

translations.literal: Taizong heard of his probity and fairness and issued an edict commending him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong heard of his probity and fairness and issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 二年，徙廣南東、西路都轉運使，尋召拜給事中。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred as chief transport commissioner of eastern and western Guangnan; soon after he was recalled as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred chief transport commissioner of eastern and western Guangnan; soon after he was recalled Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 逾月，同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: A month later he became Privy Council Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he became Privy Council Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 惟清倜儻自任，有鉤距。

translations.literal: Weiqing was bold and self-reliant, skilled in calculation and leverage.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqing was bold and self-reliant, skilled in calculation and leverage.

sentences.zh: 臨事峻刻，所至稱強幹。

translations.literal: In affairs he was harsh and exacting; wherever he served he was called a forceful administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In affairs he was harsh and exacting; wherever he served he was called a forceful administrator.

sentences.zh: 然以俗吏進，無人望。

translations.literal: Yet he had risen from the ranks of routine clerks and commanded no public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had risen from the ranks of routine clerks and commanded no public esteem.

sentences.zh: 才數月，真宗即位，加刑部侍郎，復除御史中丞。

translations.literal: Only months later Zhenzong ascended; Weiqing was made Vice Minister of Justice and again appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Only months later Zhenzong ascended; Weiqing was made Vice Minister of Justice and again appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 既去樞要，怫鬱尤甚，肆情彈擊。

translations.literal: Removed from the center of power, he was deeply frustrated and indulged in impeachments at will.
translations.idiomatic: Removed from the center of power, he was deeply frustrated and indulged in impeachments at will.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianping.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十六，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-six; posthumously honored as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged fifty-six, and was posthumously honored Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子永錫，蔭至光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: His son Yongxi inherited office as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongxi inherited office as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 頗涉學屬辭，尚氣少檢，喜交結。

translations.literal: He had some learning and facility with words, was proud and undisciplined, and liked to cultivate connections.
translations.idiomatic: He had some learning and facility with words, was proud and undisciplined, and liked to cultivate connections.

sentences.zh: 馮拯、王濟、皇甫選多與之遊，日聚舉子於家，談議時政。

translations.literal: Feng Zheng, Wang Ji, Huangfu Xuan, and others often associated with him; daily he gathered examination candidates at home to discuss current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zheng, Wang Ji, Huangfu Xuan, and others often associated with him; daily he gathered examination candidates at home to discuss current affairs.

sentences.zh: 真宗將幸河朔，永錫猶服父喪，上章大言，列詆近臣，自謂有致太平滅敵之術。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong was about to tour Hebei, Yongxi was still in mourning for his father; he submitted a bombastic memorial maligning close ministers and claiming he possessed the art of bringing peace and destroying the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong was about to tour Hebei, Yongxi was still in mourning for his father; he submitted a bombastic memorial maligning close ministers and claiming he possessed the art of bringing peace and destroying the enemy.

sentences.zh: 選為戶部判官，因對，袖表以獻，又自薦揚。

translations.literal: Selected as vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, on audience he pulled a memorial from his sleeve and also praised himself.
translations.idiomatic: Selected vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, on audience he pulled a memorial from his sleeve and also praised himself.

sentences.zh: 真宗駐蹕大名，召赴行在，試策不中，貶瀧水縣主簿。

translations.literal: Zhenzong halted at Daming and summoned him to the traveling palace; he failed the examination essay and was demoted to registrar of Longshui County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong halted at Daming and summoned him to the traveling palace; he failed the examination essay and was demoted registrar of Longshui County.

sentences.zh: 選為南劍州團練副使，俄復光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: He was selected as vice military commissioner of Nanjian Prefecture; before long he was restored as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected vice military commissioner of Nanjian Prefecture; before long he was restored vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 六年，又坐交遊非類，監和州商稅，後至右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was again punished for associating with unsuitable company, was made supervisor of commercial taxes at Hezhou, and later rose to Right Supplements Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was again punished for keeping unsuitable company, was assigned to supervise commercial taxes at Hezhou, and later rose to Right Supplements Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 次子永德，至殿中丞。

translations.literal: His second son Yongde rose to Palace Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Yongde rose to serve as Palace Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 論曰：張宏為樞副，當用兵之際，循默備位；

translations.literal: The historians comment: Zhang Hong served as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. At a time when troops were being deployed, he was silent and merely held his post.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Zhang Hong served as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. At a time when troops were being deployed, he kept silent and merely held his post.

sentences.zh: 趙昌言為御史中丞，屢上書言兵，乃兩易之。

translations.literal: Zhao Changyan was Censor-in-Chief and repeatedly submitted memorials on military affairs, so the two exchanged positions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Changyan was Censor-in-Chief and repeatedly submitted memorials on military affairs, so the two exchanged positions.

sentences.zh: 中丞可使循默者居之乎？

translations.literal: Can the post of Censor-in-Chief be filled by one who is silent and merely holds his place?
translations.idiomatic: Can the post of Censor-in-Chief be filled by a man who keeps silent and merely holds his place?

sentences.zh: 宋失政矣。

translations.literal: The Song had failed in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Here was a failure of Song governance.

sentences.zh: 昌言識李沆，器王旦；

translations.literal: Changyan recognized Li Hang's talent and valued Wang Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan recognized Li Hang's talent and valued Wang Dan.

sentences.zh: 陳恕取士得王曾，舉代得寇準；

translations.literal: Chen Shu in selecting officials obtained Wang Zeng, and in recommending a successor obtained Kou Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shu in selecting officials obtained Wang Zeng, and in recommending a successor obtained Kou Zhun.

sentences.zh: 皆可謂知人之明。

translations.literal: All may be called clear-sighted in knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: All may be called clear-sighted in judging men.

sentences.zh: 然趙好獎拔，而頗樹黨與，終以取敗；

translations.literal: Yet Zhao loved to promote and encourage others and rather formed factions, and in the end brought ruin upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhao loved to promote and encourage others and rather formed factions, and in the end brought ruin upon himself.

sentences.zh: 陳典貢舉，務黜南士，以避嫌疑，皆非君子所為也。

translations.literal: Chen presided over examinations and deliberately excluded southern scholars to avoid suspicion — none of this was conduct befitting a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Chen presided over examinations and deliberately excluded southern scholars to avoid suspicion — none of this was conduct befitting a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 昌言尚氣敢言，恕為宋人能吏之首，庶足稱矣。

translations.literal: Changyan was spirited and dared to speak out; Shu was foremost among capable administrators of the Song — both may fairly be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan was spirited and dared to speak out; Shu was foremost among capable administrators of the Song — both may fairly be praised.

sentences.zh: 劉昌言感趙普之遇，身後經理其家；

translations.literal: Liu Changyan was grateful for Zhao Pu's favor and after Pu's death managed his household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyan was grateful for Zhao Pu's favor and after Pu's death managed his household affairs.

sentences.zh: 然委親鄉里，十年而不迎侍，厚薄失措，又何取乎？

translations.literal: Yet he left his parents in their home district and for ten years did not bring them to live with him — failing in the proper measure of affection. What is there to admire in that?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he left his parents in their home district and for ten years did not bring them to live with him — failing in the proper measure of affection. What is there to admire in that?

sentences.zh: 張洎初勸李煜勿降，既而不能死之，「犬吠非主」之對，徒以辯舌，僥幸得免。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji at first urged Li Yu not to surrender, yet afterward could not die for his cause. His reply that 'a dog barks not at its own master' relied only on clever speech, and by luck he escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji at first urged Li Yu not to surrender, yet afterward could not die for his cause. His reply that 'a dog barks not at its own master' relied only on clever speech, and by luck he escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 厥後揣摩百端，讒毀正直，利口之士，鮮不為反覆小人也。

translations.literal: Thereafter he schemed in every way and slandered the upright. Men of glib tongues are rarely anything but fickle petty characters.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he schemed in every way and slandered the upright. Men of glib tongues are rarely anything but fickle petty characters.

sentences.zh: 李惟清居臺端，恨失政柄，恣情鷙擊。

translations.literal: Li Weiqing held office at the head of the censorate, resented the loss of political power, and struck out fiercely as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Weiqing held office at the head of the censorate, resented the loss of political power, and struck out fiercely as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 舊史稱為俗吏，又奚責焉。

translations.literal: The earlier history called him a vulgar official — what more is there to demand of him?
translations.idiomatic: The earlier history called him a vulgar official — what more is there to demand of him?
